items.title: ＣＮＮなど3社、国連でトランプ氏取材続行　ホワイトハウス排除で審理控え
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Helen Coster

[ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領に所属記者のホワイトハウスへの立ち入りを禁止された米メディアのＣＮＮ、ＭＳ
items.body:
Helen Coster

[ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領に所属記者のホワイトハウスへの立ち入りを禁止された米メディアのＣＮＮ、ＭＳ ＮＯＷ、ポリティコは２２日、国連が発行した記者証を使ってトランプ氏の国連出席の様子を取材した。３社はトランプ氏による排除方針を巡り、２３日に法廷審理を控える。

トランプ氏は２２日、国連本部に入る際、集まった記者団に対し「ＣＮＮが取材しに来ているとは驚いた。ここにいるべきではない。取材しないと言ったはずだ」と述べた。

ＣＮＮはトランプ氏の取材を中止するとは述べていない。

トランプ氏は１８日に３社をホワイトハウスから排除する方針を表明し、他の報道機関も締め出す可能性を示唆。これを受け、３社は２１日、合衆国憲法修正第１条で保障された言論・報道の自由を侵害しているとして、トランプ政権を提訴した。

こうした動きを巡り、ルビオ国務長官は２２日、ＮＢＣの「トゥデー」に出演し、大統領が報道内容を気に入らないという理由でメディアを締め出してよいかとの質問に対し、３社は締め出されていないと事実に反する主張を展開。「彼らは排除されていない。（中略）ＣＮＮを締め出しているわけではない。ただホワイトハウスの作業スペースからの取材が認められないだけだ」と述べた。

items.title: Ações sobem com otimismo por potenciais negociações entre EUA e Irã
items.author: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Purvi Agarwal
items.creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Purvi Agarwal
items.summary: As ações europeias fecharam em alta nesta terça-feira, com os investidores acompanhando os desdobramentos das tensões entre os Estados Unidos e o Irã, que podem influenciar os preços do petróleo e o apetite por risco.
items.body:
As ações europeias fecharam em alta nesta terça-feira, com os investidores acompanhando os desdobramentos das tensões entre os Estados Unidos e o Irã, que podem influenciar os preços do petróleo e o apetite por risco.
O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) encerrou com alta de 0,1%, após registrar na segunda-feira o maior ganho diário em mais de dois meses.
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, falando em discurso na Assembleia Geral da ONU, pediu o isolamento econômico total do Irã, sem demonstrar intenção de retomar as negociações. No entanto, ele previu que um acordo pode ser alcançado após as eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA, em novembro. Os comentários foram feitos dias depois de ele ter dado a entender que poderia se reunir com seu homólogo iraniano.
A guerra com o Irã é profundamente impopular nos EUA, com o índice de aprovação de Trump caindo para um nível recorde de baixa, à medida que a inflação atinge o bolso dos norte-americanos.
“Embora ainda haja esperanças de que possa haver algum tipo de avanço nos bastidores da conferência da ONU... ainda há muita cautela quanto à complexidade que a guerra no Irã assumiu”, disse Susannah Streeter, estrategista-chefe de investimentos do Wealth Club.
As expectativas de um avanço diplomático e relatos de que o Irã se ofereceu para reabrir o Estreito de Ormuz em até sete dias ajudaram a empurrar os preços do petróleo para as mínimas de duas semanas. As ações do setor de energia europeu (.SXEP) reverteram as quedas anteriores e fecharam com alta de 0,2%.
A maioria dos setores do STOXX 600 registrou alta, liderados pelo de varejo (.SXRP) , que registrou seu maior ganho em um único dia desde o início de abril.
Em LONDRES, o índice Financial Times (.FTSE) recuou 0,29%, a 10.708,33 pontos.
Em FRANKFURT, o índice DAX (.GDAXI) subiu 0,02%, a 25.578,85 pontos.
Em PARIS, o índice CAC-40 (.FCHI) ganhou 0,20%, a 8.154,91 pontos.
Em MILÃO, o índice Ftse/Mib (.FTMIB) teve desvalorização de 0,53%, a 52.095,83 pontos.
Em MADRI, o índice Ibex-35 (.IBEX) registrou alta de 0,15%, a 19.754,10 pontos.
Em LISBOA, o índice PSI20 (.PSI20) valorizou-se 0,41%, a 9.656,71 pontos.

items.title: Nigeria wins arbitration as Sunrise's $400 million hydropower claim dismissed
items.author: Camillus Eboh
items.creator: Camillus Eboh
items.summary: Nigeria has won an international arbitration case after a tribunal dismissed a $400 million claim by Sunrise Power and Transmission over the long-delayed Mambilla hydroelectric project, Attorney-General Lateef Fagbemi said on Tuesday.
items.body:
Nigeria has won an international arbitration case after a tribunal dismissed a $400 million claim by Sunrise Power and Transmission over the long-delayed Mambilla hydroelectric project, Attorney-General Lateef Fagbemi said on Tuesday.
The September 17 ruling removes a major legal obstacle to the 3,050-megawatt hydropower project, potentially reviving Nigeria's biggest hydroelectric scheme after nearly two decades of delays.
Fagbemi said the International Chamber of Commerce tribunal found that settlement agreements relied on by Sunrise were not binding on Nigeria because the officials who signed them lacked the authority to commit the government without presidential approval.
He said the tribunal also found the agreements were tainted by corruption and contrary to Nigerian public policy, making them unenforceable.
Fagbemi said Sunrise was ordered to pay 75% of Nigeria's legal fees and expenses, with 10% interest compounded annually.
Sunrise did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The ruling could clear the way for renewed efforts to advance the project, whose financing from China's Export-Import Bank had been contingent on resolving the dispute.
Fagbemi added that Sunrise is pursuing a separate arbitration claim against Nigeria worth more than $2.7 billion.

items.title: Big banks exploring Canadian dollar-based digital money with tokenized deposits
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: Canada’s big banks are exploring the development of Canadian dollar-based digital money, starting with a tokenized deposits initiative.
items.body: TORONTO — Canada’s big banks are exploring the development of Canadian dollar-based digital money, starting with a tokenized deposits initiative. Tokenized deposits are traditional bank deposits recorded on a decentralized database or distributed ledger, such as a blockchain. The plan seeks to deliver faster, more efficient and programmable payments to Canadian customers while preserving safety, stability and effective regulatory oversight. It means Canadian dollars could be converted into tokens on blockchain for easier transfers, said Claire Célérier, Canada Research Chair in household finance at the University of Toronto’s Rotman School of Management. “My understanding is that the six banks will share the same blockchain, and so it implies that transactions can be made instantaneously across wallets with tokens,” she said. The tokens would be issued by commercial banks and from a legal perspective, depositors can treat them the same as traditional bank deposits. Bank of Montreal, CIBC, National Bank, Royal Bank, Scotiabank and TD Bank are taking a collaborative approach to the project. Célérier said the potential capabilities would be of particular benefit to large companies or institutional investors, allowing them to complete “more sophisticated transactions.” “What I expect is that these tokenized dollars will be mostly used by large companies and so on who have accounts across these Canadian banks, and it will be used to move large amounts of money,” she said. Another potential benefit, Célérier said, is that it could increase the efficiency of international transfers. The banks say the first phase aims to move tokenized deposits between Canadian financial institutions. “It’s really exploratory now. I think what they’re saying is that they’re willing to work together to develop the technology,” Célérier said. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 22, 2026.

items.title: Canadian dollar hits nearly seven-week low on wider yield spreads
items.author: Fergal Smith
items.creator: Fergal Smith
items.summary: The Canadian dollar weakened to a nearly seven-week low against its U.S. counterpart on Tuesday as the gap between US and Canadian yields continued to widen despite the recent more hawkish stance of Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem.
items.body:
The Canadian dollar weakened to a nearly seven-week low against its U.S. counterpart on Tuesday as the gap between US and Canadian yields continued to widen despite the recent more hawkish stance of Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem.
The loonie was trading 0.3% lower at 1.4075 per U.S. dollar, or 71.05 US cents, after touching its weakest intraday level since August 5 at 1.4078.
"The combination of widening rate differentials, escalating trade uncertainty and bullish technical momentum is driving USD-CAD toward fresh highs," said Kevin Ford, FX & macro strategist at Convera.
"Markets have increased the probability of an October BoC hike, but Macklem’s tougher language has not offset the dollar’s growing carry advantage."
The [USN:L6N45E0MQ TEXT:"U.S. dollar"] (.DXY) rose against a basket of major currencies as investors weighed the possibility of more interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.
The Canadian 2-year yield fell 2.4 basis points further below the US equivalent to a gap of about 148 basis points in favor of the US note, marking the widest gap since March 2025.
Investors see a roughly 60% chance the BoC would hike in October. On Monday, [USN:BCLLKEM29 TEXT:"Macklem"] said that the central bank had to take into consideration the fact that while slower growth linked to new US tariffs could drag inflation downwards, the Middle East conflict could push it up as oil prices soar.
The price of oil, one of Canada's major exports, rose as traders worried about global supplies. U.S. crude [USN:L1N45E01S TEXT:"oil"] futures were trading 0.9% higher at $96.65 a barrel.
As trade uncertainties mount, Canada has sought to [USN:L6N45E04M TEXT:"diversify economic ties"] and [USN:L1N45D0UD TEXT:"speed up the approval process"] for major natural resource projects.
The Canadian 10-year yield was barely changed at 3.847%, after touching an earlier two-week low at 3.802%.

US President Donald Trump said the US may make a deal with Iran after the midterm elections, but warned that he could take stronger military action if Iran does not agree.

US President Donald Trump addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), in New York City, US, Sep 22, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Kylie Cooper)

UNITED NATIONS: US President Donald Trump used his UN General Assembly speech on Tuesday (Sep 22) to argue that t he war with Iran prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and warn that he could "annihilate t he Islamic Republic" if no deal is reac he d to end t he conflict.
While predicting his administration would strike a peace deal with Iran following t he Nov 3 US midterm elections , Trump called on ot he r nations to join America in isolating Iran economically to force it to t he negotiating table.
"I have a big decision to make. Will a deal be made with Iran that lets t he m rebuild and create a far greater co un try than it ever was before?" Trump said. "Or do I annihilate t he Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving t he m a chance to kill and destroy people and co un tries again?"
Trump added: "Do I drive t he m into he ll with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations? But I believe we'll make a deal right after t he election."

T he speech marked t he latest justification Trump has offered for t he war with Iran . He has previously cited a range of reasons for t he February US-Israeli strikes, including Tehran's nuclear program, its support for regional proxy groups and t he prospect of regime change.
Iran has consistently denied seeking to develop nuclear weapons.
Outside t he UN he adquarters, dozens of anti- Iran ian government demonstrators gat he red, a few of t he m holding up signs calling for freedom and democracy and decrying dictatorship.
"I believe we'll make a deal right after t he election because it doesn't make sense for t he m not to. T he y're waiting to see how I do in t he midterm election," Trump said during a speech to t he Un ited Nations General Assembly.

Related:

In addition to defending t he decision to attack Iran , Trump was expected to use his speech to criticize t he UN , highlighting his administration's efforts to prevent t he organization and ot he r international bodies from encroaching on US sovereignty or advancing what it views as a left-wing agenda, according to a White House official who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Trump last year caused a stir with a combative speech at t he UN , saying that ot he r co un tries were "going to he ll" for, among ot he r things, climate policy and mass migration.
T he speech kicked off a day of high-level diplomacy at t he Un ited Nations, w he re Trump was due to meet more than a dozen world leaders as wars in t he Middle East and Ukraine continued to test his foreign policy agenda.
After his speech , Trump is sc he duled to meet with no fewer than 11 world leaders, bilaterally or in group settings.
Later on Tuesday, Trump will meet with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Venezuela's interim leader Delcy Rodriguez, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen, and t he representatives of t he Gulf states of t he Un ited Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait and Qatar.
In t he evening, he may meet dozens more leaders, albeit briefly, during a leaders' reception. Trump met with French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday. Additions to his Tuesday sc he dule are possible.
T he long list of foreign leader meetings reflects t he US president's focus on foreign affairs during his second term, during which he has started multiple wars, questioned longstanding alliances, threatened allies with invasion and sought to broker well over a dozen conflicts, with mixed success.

Related:

Trump returns to UN at a moment of anxiety about Iran, AI and the future of world body itself

Commentary: Trump declares victory in Greenland, but the deal exposes a deeper crisis of trust

T he US-Israeli war against Iran has been particularly consequential, driving up fuel prices globally, dragging down Trump 's approval ratings and presenting a challenge for Republicans r un ning in t he Nov 3 congressional midterm election. On Monday, a Reuters/Ipsos poll showed Trump 's approval rating falling to an all-time low of 32 per cent, as his fellow Republicans soured on his handling of t he cost of living.
Among t he closely watc he d meetings will be t he seven-way gat he ring with t he Gulf leaders, many of whom are alarmed by t he recent advances of t he Houthis , Iran -backed militants who have captured wide swat he s of Yemen, attacked US ally Saudi Arabia and threatened shipping through t he strategic Bab el-Mandab Strait.
Political allies and opponents will also be closely watching Trump 's first-ever meeting with Venezuela's Rodriguez, who rose to power with t he Trump administration's blessing after US forces snatc he d President Nicolas Maduro in January and took him to New York to face drug trafficking charges.
Trump 's allies say t he US is working with Rodriguez to open Venezuela's oil sector to US investment, but Democrats and some Republicans say his administration has not done enough to press for new elections in t he South American nation.
During t he meeting with t he leaders of Denmark and Greenland, its overseas territory, Trump will ink an accord designed to increase US military presence on t he island while limiting that of geopolitical adversaries. Danish and Greenland officials hope t he accord will put an end to Trump 's past comments suggesting he might take Greenland by force.

Source: Reuters/fs

On Monday, a Reuters/Ipsos poll showed Trump 's approval rating falling to an all-time low of 32 per cent, as his fellow Republicans soured on his handling of t he cost of living.
Among t he closely watc he d meetings will be t he seven-way gat he ring with t he Gulf leaders, many of whom are alarmed by t he recent advances of t he Houthis , Iran -backed militants who have captured wide swat he s of Yemen, attacked US ally Saudi Arabia and threatened shipping through t he strategic Bab el-Mandab Strait.
Political allies and opponents will also be closely watching Trump 's first-ever meeting with Venezuela's Rodriguez, who rose to power with t he Trump administration's blessing after US forces snatc he d President Nicolas Maduro in January and took him to New York to face drug trafficking charges.
Trump 's allies say t he US is working with Rodriguez to open Venezuela's oil sector to US investment, but Democrats and some Republicans say his administration has not done enough to press for new elections in t he South American nation.
During t he meeting with t he leaders of Denmark and Greenland, its overseas territory, Trump will ink an accord designed to increase US military presence on t he island while limiting that of geopolitical adversaries. Danish and Greenland officials hope t he accord will put an end to Trump 's past comments suggesting he might take Greenland by force.

items.title: Wall Street holds near its record after Brent oil briefly falls below US$98 per barrel
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: Oil prices retreated for the fifth straight day Tuesday and Wall Street was poised to open modestly higher as pressure from the bond market eased.
items.body: NEW YORK — Wall Street is holding near its record high Tuesday in a relatively quiet day for markets worldwide. The S&P 500 was mostly unchanged and is sitting 0.4 per cent below its all-time high set last month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 170 points, or 0.3 per cent, as of 12:50 p.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was adding 0.3 per cent to its own record. Stocks had been higher in the morning, when the price for a barrel of Brent crude briefly fell below $98. But oil prices later trimmed their losses, and Brent was most recently at $100.19 per barrel. That’s down from the nearly $110 that it touched last week, but it’s still much more expensive than the $72 it was fetching before the war with Iran began. It’s been swinging with uncertainty about when the war will allow crude to freely flow again from the Middle East to customers worldwide. On Wall Street, AutoZone rose 6 per cent after the retailer reported a stronger profit for the latest quarter than analysts expected, though its revenue fell short. CEO Phil Daniele said the auto parts seller faced “a difficult selling environment” in the first two months of the quarter, but it improved afterward and “we feel we are well positioned for sales growth” in its upcoming fiscal year. At Thor Industries, which sells recreational vehicles, the mood was more muted. CEO Bob Martin said expensive fuel, high interest rates and still-high inflation are stretching its customers’ budgets, and business “never reached the inflection point many in the industry expected” in its latest fiscal year. Its stock rose 4.7 per cent, though, after it delivered a stronger profit for the latest quarter than analysts expected. Such strong profit reports are one of the main reasons the U.S. stock market has reached the brink of its all-time high despite high oil prices and jitters about whether stocks in the artificial-intelligence industry shot too high. Many companies are close to closing the books on their third quarter of the year, which ends with September. And analysts are forecasting companies in the S&P 500 will report overall growth of nearly 29 per cent for the quarter from a year earlier, according to FactSet. If they’re right, it would be the third straight quarter of growth better than 25 per cent for the index. And stock prices tend to follow the track of corporate profits over the long term. On Holding’s stock that trades in the United States jumped 10.6 per cent after the Swiss sneaker and sportswear company unveiled its financial goals for upcoming years. It also approved a plan to buy back up to $1 billion of its stock through 2029. Such purchases send cash directly to investors and boost the company’s per-share performance. On the losing end of Wall Street were several stocks of companies in the oil and gas industry, which were hurt by the drop in crude prices. ConocoPhillips slipped 0.8 per cent. Banks also dropped, continuing their weak run since last week, when the Federal Reserve raised the overnight interest rate that it controls for the first time in three years. When the spread narrows between short-term interest rates and longer ones, banks come under pressure because they make profit off the difference. JPMorgan Chase fell 3.4 per cent and was one of the heaviest weights on the S&P 500. The gap between short- and long-term yields in the bond market did not move much, as the 10-year Treasury yield inched up to 4.98 per cent from 4.96 per cent late Monday. Like oil prices, it also remains far above where it was before the war with Iran began, when it was at 3.97 per cent. In stock markets abroad, indexes ticked higher across much of Europe and Asia. London’s FTSE 100 was an outlier and dipped 0.3 per cent. Stocks rose 0.2 per cent in Hong Kong and 0.1 per cent in Shanghai after Alibaba unveiled new artificial intelligence chip technologies, including what it said was China’s most powerful AI chip. That comes just days ahead of a meeting between Chinese and U.S. leaders at which competition to lead on AI technology is expected to be a major theme. ___ AP Business Writer Yuri Kageyama contributed to this report.

items.title: トルコ大統領、国連改革求める　サウジ・フーシ派停戦へ仲介継続
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [アンカラ ２２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[アンカラ ２２日 ロイター] - トルコのエルドアン大統領は２２日、国連総会で演説し、国連は平和維持の責務を果たせなくなっていると指摘した上で、安全保障理事会の改革を求めた。

エルドアン氏は数年前から、安保理をより包括的で幅広い構造にするよう求めてきた。「１９０カ国以上の意思が５カ国の気まぐれに左右される制度は、公平でもなければ、信頼を十分に築くことができるものでもないと認識するべきだ」と述べた。また、「８１年前に設立された国連は、この使命を果たせなくなっている。むしろ、果たせないようにされてしまった」と続けた。

エルドアン氏はパレスチナ自治区ガザの状況も非難し、「良心を持つ者ならば、現地で起きていることに目を背けることはできない」と語った。

パレスチナ自治政府のアッバス議長が２年連続で国連総会の場に姿を見せられていないことについても不当だと批判。パレスチナ国家を承認していない国々に再考を促し、全ての国に対し、ガザでの戦争終結に向けてイスラエルへの圧力を強めるよう呼びかけた。

エルドアン氏はまた、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派とサウジアラビアの戦闘を終結させるため、トルコが全ての関係者と協力して努力を続けていると述べ、戦闘の継続は誰の利益にもならないと強調した。

その上で、トルコは紛争終結に向けた外交努力を維持していくと表明した。

フーシ派は、イエメンで戦闘が再び激化する中、サウジアラビアへの攻撃を強めている。

items.title: CNN, CBS News oversight board will be 'toothless,' experts warn
items.author: Jaspreet Singh
items.creator: Jaspreet Singh
items.summary: David Ellison is set to take control of two of the biggest news organizations in the US after his Paramount Skydance completes its takeover of Warner Bros Discovery , giving him wide influence over the news media landscape. But experts warn his promise of editorial independence for CNN and CBS News is a hollow one.
items.body:
David Ellison is set to [USN:L4N45D112 TEXT:"take control"] of two of the biggest news organizations in the US after his Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) completes its takeover of Warner Bros Discovery (WBD.O) , giving him wide influence over the news media landscape. But experts warn his promise of editorial independence for CNN and CBS News is a hollow one.
Ellison agreed to create an editorial independence board to oversee CNN and CBS as part of Monday's [USN:L4N45D1A9 TEXT:"settlement"] with a coalition of 12 US states and a Hollywood writers' union. The group will be made up of five veteran journalists, to "establish guiding editorial and journalism principles for the combined entity's news channels," according to the agreement.
[USN:L6N45D0SG TEXT:"Skepticism abounds"]. "Genuine oversight of a news organization is provided by its editors and owners. If they are not committed to doing things honorably themselves, nobody they appoint and pay can possibly be expected to do it for them," said Dan Gillmor, a retired journalist and educator.
"Of course" the board will be toothless, he said.
Notably, the board, whose members will be appointed and paid by the combined entity, is not explicitly granted investigative oversight and the binding nature of its decisions is unclear, leaving final authority in the hands of Ellison.
Some of CNN's current and former staff are also questioning the settlement. Prominent journalist Kara Swisher said earlier this year that she plans to leave the network "as soon as I can" due to the Paramount takeover and dismissing the independence board as a "fig leaf."
"Ellison's record at CBS so far is not encouraging and is even troubling. I think he is a very pleasant person, … That hardly matters, as I am only interested in how he behaves as a media owner. So far, I am not impressed," Swisher told Reuters.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta said the board is a meaningful way to protect the integrity of CNN and CBS.
'ENFORCEMENT GAPS' The settlement also creates [USN:L4N45D1A9 TEXT:"an independent monitoring trustee"] with broad authority over film production and cable-licensing, but the trustee shall have "no role or authority relating to the Combined Entity's news operations."
"That's a remarkable carveout," said Jonathan Peters, a media law professor at the University of Georgia.
He said the settlement is not without legal merit because states have the power to enforce it in federal court, but there is a "significant enforcement gap" regarding editorial independence.
The concerns are also fueled by [USN:L1N43G107 TEXT:"lawmakers' criticism of Ellison"] for tailoring news coverage at Paramount-owned CBS News to favor President Donald Trump. Critics fear how he would manage Warner's CNN once it comes under his ownership.
There is also no provision that requires the board's findings and decisions to be made public.
The companies said the board would also resolve internal disputes over reporting bias and disputes between news staff and management at CNN and CBS.
Board members will serve three-year terms and are protected against arbitrary dismissal by a "good cause" removal standard, though the company retains exclusive authority to fill all vacancies.
"It's unclear how the attorneys general or courts can constitutionally hold Paramount accountable for the board's actions or inaction without themselves interfering in content," said Seth Stern, a media lawyer and chief of advocacy at the Freedom of the Press Foundation.
WALL STREET JOURNAL PRECEDENT The new owner will get about a six-month window to reshape newsroom leadership before any oversight begins, as the board will be established only within 180 days of the merger.
The idea of an independent oversight board is not new. When Rupert Murdoch's News Corp (NWSA.O) bought the Wall Street Journal in 2007, it agreed to establish a special committee to protect the objectivity and independence of its publications.
The group is meant to guard against corporate interference and it must approve changes to the Journal's top editors, but it does not assess or comment on editorial coverage.
Even so, it is considered powerless.
"When Murdoch wanted to install his own loyal lieutenant as top editor in 2008, he just did it, the board was left in the dust," Bill Grueskin, a faculty member at Columbia Journalism School and former deputy managing editor of the Wall Street Journal, said in an emailed response.
Grueskin sees little difference in Ellison's concessions to editorial independence.
"The owner calls the shots," he said. "The responsibilities and rights of Ellison's board are exceptionally vague.

items.title: Retornos bonos Tesoro EEUU suben levemente, inversores evalúan expectativas de alza de tasas de Fed
items.author: Caroline Valetkevitch
items.creator: Caroline Valetkevitch
items.summary: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subían ligeramente el martes, mientras los inversores sopesaban la caída de los precios del petróleo frente a las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba nuevamente las tasas de interés.
items.body:
Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subían ligeramente el martes, mientras los inversores sopesaban la caída de los precios del petróleo frente a las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba nuevamente las tasas de interés.
El retorno a dos años, que suele evolucionar en consonancia con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, alcanzó un nuevo máximo de dos años, situándose en el 4,7879%.
La Fed subió el costo del crédito la semana pasada por primera vez desde 2023 para intentar controlar la inflación. Los operadores estiman que hay aproximadamente un 53% de probabilidad de otro incremento cuando el banco central se reúna en octubre, según CME FedWatch.
La presidenta de la Fed de Boston, Susan Collins, escribió el martes en LinkedIn que apoyaba la decisión tomada la semana pasada por el banco central de subir las tasas ante los riesgos de que la inflación futura se sitúe sobre el 2%.
Los precios del petróleo bajaban, pero se mantenían sobre los mínimos del día. Los precios del crudo se han disparado desde el inicio de la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, lo que ha avivado el temor a la inflación y a un aumento de las tasas de interés.
Los inversionistas también asimilaban los comentarios del presidente Donald Trump, quien dijo ante las Naciones Unidas que creía que Estados Unidos llegaría a un acuerdo con Irán justo después de que se celebren las elecciones legislativas de noviembre.
Los rendimientos de referencia a 10 años subían marginalmente, pero se mantenían bajo el 5%, tras haber alcanzado el 5,041% la semana pasada, el máximo desde 2007. Ganaban 0,7 puntos básicos, a 4,97%. La rentabilidad a 30 años sumaba 0,7 puntos básicos, al 5,303%.
El retorno a dos años sumaba 0,69 puntos básicos, al 4,76%.
Más tarde, este martes, el Tesoro subastará 69.000 millones de dólares en títulos del Tesoro a dos años. También se esperan subastas a cinco y siete años esta semana.
Un indicador muy seguido de la curva de rendimientos, que mide la diferencia entre las tasas a dos y 10 años , y que se considera un indicador de las expectativas económicas, se situaba en 21,4 puntos básicos.

items.title: Trump dice que Departamento de Justicia podría tomar medidas contra empresas de IA si es necesario
items.author: Courtney Rozen, Gram Slattery
items.creator: Courtney Rozen, Gram Slattery
items.summary: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, reiteró su oposición a las nuevas regulaciones sobre la tecnología de inteligencia artificial y declaró el martes ante los líderes mundiales reunidos en la Asamblea General de la ONU que, en caso necesario, las fuerzas del orden de su país tomarían medidas para controlar el sector.
items.body:
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, reiteró su oposición a las nuevas regulaciones sobre la tecnología de inteligencia artificial y declaró el martes ante los líderes mundiales reunidos en la Asamblea General de la ONU que, en caso necesario, las fuerzas del orden de su país tomarían medidas para controlar el sector.
"Vamos a vigilarlo de cerca a través del Departamento de Justicia", afirmó Trump, refiriéndose a la tecnología de la IA y a la principal agencia de las fuerzas del orden de Estados Unidos.
La alarma pública sobre el peligro potencial que plantea la IA va en aumento, después de que el investigador de Anthropic Jacob Coxon dimitiera y afirmara que "las personas que desarrollan la IA creen sinceramente que podría matarnos a todos antes de que termine la década".
En las últimas semanas, Trump ha restado importancia a las alertas sobre la IA, argumentando que tales afirmaciones son un "engaño".
"No voy a frenar el crecimiento de algo que será más importante que la Revolución Industrial", afirmó.
Trump también señaló que, en adelante, los documentos del Gobierno de Estados Unidos utilizarán el término "superinteligencia" en lugar de "inteligencia artificial".

items.summary: Exor , the investment arm of Italy's billionaire Agnelli family, announced a share buyback of €500 million ($572 million) on Tuesday.
items.body:
Exor (EXOR.AS) , the investment arm of Italy's billionaire Agnelli family, announced a share buyback of €500 million ($572 million) on Tuesday.
The group said its deployable cash position would rise to around €4 billion, including proceeds from the sale of its interest in Iveco and the planned disposal of Welltec. Exor also reported:
A first-half net asset value of €157.9 per share, a decrease of 3.9% from a year earlier..
A first-half gross asset value of €35.77 billion, down 3.7%.
A loan-to-value (LTV) ratio of 4.7%
Exor's holdings span sectors including autos, healthcare, media and sports through investments in Stellantis (STLAM.MI) , Ferrari (RACE.MI) , Philips (PHG.AS) , Juventus (JUVE.MI) and The Economist.

items.title: Bolsas europeas suben por expectativas de conversaciones entre EEUU e Irán
items.author: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Purvi Agarwal
items.creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Purvi Agarwal
items.summary: Las bolsas europeas cerraron ligeramente al alza el martes, mientras los inversores seguían de cerca la evolución de la tensión entre Estados Unidos e Irán, que podría influir en los precios del petróleo y en el apetito por el riesgo.
items.body:
Las bolsas europeas cerraron ligeramente al alza el martes, mientras los inversores seguían de cerca la evolución de la tensión entre Estados Unidos e Irán, que podría influir en los precios del petróleo y en el apetito por el riesgo.
El índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 (.STOXX) ganó un 0,1%, tras haber anotado el lunes su mayor subida diaria en más de dos meses. La mayoría de las principales bolsas regionales también cerraron al alza.
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, en su intervención ante la Asamblea General de la ONU, pidió el aislamiento económico total de Irán, sin mostrar ninguna intención de reanudar las negociaciones.
Sin embargo, predijo que podría alcanzarse un acuerdo tras las elecciones legislativas de noviembre. Los comentarios ocurrieron días después de que insinuó que podría reunirse con su par iraní.
La guerra con Irán es profundamente impopular en Estados Unidos, donde la aprobación a Trump ha caído a mínimos históricos a medida que la inflación afecta al poder adquisitivo de los estadounidenses.
"Aunque aún persisten las esperanzas de que pueda haber algún tipo de avance entre bastidores en la conferencia de la ONU (...) sigue habiendo mucha cautela respecto a lo compleja que se ha vuelto la guerra en Irán", dijo Susannah Streeter, estratega jefe de inversiones de Wealth Club.
Las esperanzas de un avance diplomático y reportes de que Irán ha ofrecido a reabrir el estrecho de Ormuz en un plazo de siete días contribuyeron a que los precios del petróleo cayesen a mínimos de dos semanas. Las acciones del sector energético europeo (.SXEP) revirtieron las bajas previas y subieron un 0,2%.
La mayoría de los sectores del STOXX 600 avanzaron, liderados por el minorista (.SXRP) , que anotaba su mayor subida diaria desde inicios de abril, en gran medida por la escalda del 12,4% de Kingfisher (KGF.L) , luego de que la cadena de bricolaje revisó al alza sus previsiones para el año.
Las acciones tecnológicas (.SX8P) ganaban un 1,5%, siguiendo el ejemplo del Nasdaq estadounidense, que alcanzó un máximo histórico intradía.
Las subidas generales se vieron limitadas por una caída del 1% de los valores bancarios (.SX7P) . Las acciones del sector de las telecomunicaciones (.SXKP) perdieron un 2,1%, y Ericsson (ERICb.ST) se hundió un 3,8%, después de que Morgan Stanley bajó la calificación del fabricante sueco de equipos de telecomunicaciones.

items.title: Beats 360: precio, batería y cómo son los nuevos auriculares personalizables de Apple
items.author: Chris Welch
items.summary: Los nuevos Beats 360 llegan con cancelación activa de ruido, hasta 32 horas de batería y compatibilidad con funciones de Android.
items.body: Bloomberg — La marca Beats, de Apple Inc. ( AAPL ), anunció unos nuevos auriculares inalámbricos de gama alta que permiten a los usuarios cambiar entre almohadillas y diademas, disponibles en una amplia gama de colores y materiales, lo que ofrece cientos de opciones de personalización. Los Beats 360, con un precio de US$350 y disponibles en las tiendas a partir del jueves, presentan un diseño ligero y son el primer modelo supraauricular de la marca que ofrece una auténtica resistencia al agua y al sudor, aunque los modelos anteriores ya son habituales en los gimnasios. En comparación con otros auriculares de Beats, los 360 presentan un diseño novedoso y distintivo. La marca se inspiró en la cultura de las zapatillas deportivas en su esfuerzo por hacer que los auriculares 360 fueran más personalizables que sus modelos anteriores, según afirmó Oliver Schusser, vicepresidente de Apple a cargo de Beats y Apple Music, en una rueda de prensa celebrada antes del anuncio del martes. Ver más: Bose apuesta por audífonos que parecen un pendiente: nuevos modelos desde US$199 y hasta US$299 La marca apuesta a que el énfasis en el estilo y la personalización ayudará a diferenciar los Beats 360 en el saturado segmento de los auriculares con cancelación de ruido, que incluye productos de precio similar de Sony Group Corp. ( SONY ), Bose Corp. y otras marcas. Sony ha relanzado recientemente sus populares auriculares WH-1000XM4, lanzados originalmente en 2020, que ofrecen el último estándar Bluetooth, una batería sustituible por el usuario y un ajuste de audio modernizado por US$300. Los Beats 360 son compatibles con el audio espacial Dolby Atmos, incorporan una cancelación activa de ruido más potente que la de los auriculares Studio Pro lanzados en 2023 y ofrecen hasta 32 horas de reproducción. Cinco minutos de carga deberían proporcionar una hora de tiempo de reproducción. A diferencia de los AirPods Max 2 de Apple, que cuestan US$549 y están dirigidos principalmente a consumidores integrados en el ecosistema de Apple, los Beats 360 también son compatibles con funciones de Android como Fast Pair, el cambio fluido de audio y Find Hub. Ver más: Samsung lanza el Galaxy S26 con más funciones de IA y nuevos audífonos: precios Los últimos auriculares de Beats son más ligeros y tienen un volumen más alto que los Studio Pro, además de contar con una arquitectura acústica más avanzada que les confiere un campo sonoro más amplio, unos graves más profundos y una mayor claridad general. La marca seguirá comercializando los auriculares Studio Pro a un precio más bajo, de US$300 dólares. Beats ofrece los auriculares 360 en cuatro colores: negro, blanco, azul y rosa. Cada modelo incluye almohadillas de punto de alto rendimiento a juego. También se comercializan almohadillas sueltas en azul marino y amarillo brillante. El modelo ultra plush solo está disponible en negro o blanco. Según ha indicado la marca, los clientes podrán disponer de otros colores en el futuro. Durante una promoción de lanzamiento por tiempo limitado, los kits de almohadillas y diadema de los Beats 360 estarán disponibles por US$10, un precio reducido diseñado para animar a los compradores a adquirir más de un modelo. El precio de los kits aumentará posteriormente hasta los US$50 dólares. Los auriculares intercambiables se acoplan con un sencillo movimiento de giro, mientras que la diadema encaja en su sitio mediante clips. Se puede elegir entre dos materiales diferentes para las almohadillas: un tejido “de punto técnico” transpirable, ideal para entrenar o correr, mientras que el ultra plush resulta más adecuado para el uso diario. Ver más: Esto cuestan los audífonos Montblanc que redefinen la elegancia del sonido En las pruebas que he realizado hasta ahora, he comprobado que la posibilidad de cambiar rápidamente entre ambos materiales permite utilizar un único par de auriculares Beats 360 para diferentes actividades a lo largo del día, en lugar de necesitar un par específico para hacer ejercicio. Los auriculares detectan automáticamente qué material se está utilizando en cada momento y ajustan la configuración acústica para ofrecer el mejor rendimiento de audio. Hay al menos dos inconvenientes que podrían disuadir a algunos compradores potenciales: los Beats 360 no admiten la reproducción con cable, por lo que se está limitado al audio inalámbrico por Bluetooth en todo momento. Esto significa que no hay forma de disfrutar de un sonido sin pérdidas de alta fidelidad. Tampoco se incluye ningún cable USB-C en la caja. Hasta el momento, los auriculares Beats 360 han demostrado ser muy cómodos y presentar una buena distribución del peso, aunque es posible que los usuarios con cabezas de mayor tamaño echen en falta un mayor margen de ajuste en los auriculares: a mí apenas me quedan bien en la longitud máxima. Cambiar las almohadillas no requiere apenas esfuerzo, aunque la diadema puede resultar un poco más complicada de ajustar correctamente. Al igual que en ocasiones anteriores, Beats ha distribuido los nuevos auriculares entre famosos, personas influyentes y deportistas antes de su lanzamiento, con el fin de generar expectación inicial y despertar el interés de los consumidores. Han aparecido en eventos como el Mundial de Fútbol y el US Open, y Kendall Jenner será la imagen de una nueva campaña de marketing que incluye una serie de anuncios en los que se destaca el estilo personalizable de los auriculares. items.title: Clemson-Georgia cancel future 4-game series
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A four-game football series scheduled between Georgia and Clemson has been called off.
items.body:
A four-game football series scheduled between Georgia and Clemson has been called off.
That's according to a report late Monday from the Athens Banner-Herald. The games had been set for 2029, 2030, 2032 and 2033.
The schools quietly canceled the series in March with a signed agreement, the newspaper reported after receiving a copy of the document through an open records request.
"The parties have mutually agreed to terminate the Contracts and all of the provisions of those contracts, including payment requirements," the document read.
Neither school has confirmed the cancellation.
The reason for calling off the series is unknown. The original agreements were made in 2018 and 2019, when Clemson was winning national championships and Georgia was a program on the rise.
Clemson played in four College Football Playoff championship games in five years from 2016-20, winning twice. Georgia lost the title game for the 2017 season, then won back-to-back titles in 2022 and '23.
The shift by the Southeastern Conference, of which Georgia is a member, to a nine-game conference schedule in 2026 has impacted the Bulldogs' plan for nonconference games.
Georgia previously canceled home-and-home series with Louisville for 2026 and 2027, Florida State in 2027 and 2028, and NC State in 2033 and 2034.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Fed's Barkin says economy may be firming, inflation not limited to energy, tariff shocks
items.author: Howard Schneider
items.creator: Howard Schneider
items.summary: US economic conditions "are, if anything, firming," with continued consumer spending and strength beyond the boom in artificial intelligence keeping the Federal Reserve's focus on inflation, Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said on Tuesday.
items.body:
US economic conditions "are, if anything, firming," with continued consumer spending and strength beyond the boom in artificial intelligence keeping the Federal Reserve's focus on inflation, Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said on Tuesday.
"The risks to inflation outweigh the risks to maximum employment. That's why we [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"raised rates"]," at last week's meeting, Barkin said in comments prepared for delivery to the CFA Society Baltimore, adding that the quarter-percentage-point hike "will help" restore inflation to the Fed's 2% target.
"Will additional hikes be required, and how many? We'll see," said Barkin, who is not a voting member of the central bank's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee this year.
The Fed last week raised its policy interest rate to the 3.75%-4.00% range, with investors anticipating more increases.
Barkin's comments follow those of other Fed officials who have broadened their concerns about inflation that they feel is being driven increasingly by strong demand in the economy, and not just by energy, tariff and other supply issues that might be expected to fade on their own.
Even those "'passing' shocks aren't proving to be short-lived, or one-off events," but are producing more persistent price pressures than at first expected, Barkin said.
"It is tempting to try to blame high inflation on a handful of categories with particularly high exposure to the Middle East conflict or to tariffs," he said. But much of the [USN:L1N44N0KC TEXT:"Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index"] is increasing at greater than a 3% annual rate.
"I am hearing momentum outside of data centers, too. The defense sector is hot. Manufacturing contacts are starting to sound more upbeat. Bankers tell us pipelines are healthy," Barkin said.

items.title: Fed's Barkin says economy may be firming, inflation not limited to energy, tariff shocks
items.author: By Howard Schneider
items.summary: By Howard Schneider BALTIMORE, Sept 22 (Reuters) - US economic conditions "are, if anything, firming," with continued consumer spending and strength beyond t...
items.body:
Fed's Barkin says economy may be firming, inflation not limited to energy, tariff shocks

1 / 11
Fed's Barkin says economy may be firming, inflation not limited to energy, tariff shocks Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond President Thomas Barkin looks on at the Economic Club of Washington DC in Washington, D.C., U.S., April 9, 2025. REUTERS/Kevin Mohatt

By Howard Schneider
Tue, September 22, 2026 at 12:52 PM EDT 2 min read

By Howard Schneider
BALTIMORE, Sept 22 (Reuters) - US economic conditions "are, if anything, firming," with continued consumer spending and strength beyond the boom in artificial intelligence keeping the Federal Reserve's focus on inflation, Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said on Tuesday.
"The risks to inflation outweigh the risks to maximum employment. That's why we raised rates," at last week's meeting, Barkin said in comments prepared for delivery to the CFA Society Baltimore, adding that the quarter-percentage-point hike "will help" restore inflation to the Fed's 2% target.

"Will additional hikes be required, and how many? We'll see," said Barkin, who is not a voting member of the central bank's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee this year.
The Fed last week raised its policy interest rate to the 3.75%-4.00% range, with investors anticipating more increases.
Barkin's comments follow those of other Fed officials who have broadened their concerns about inflation that they feel is being driven increasingly by strong demand in the economy, and not just by energy, tariff and other supply issues that might be expected to fade on their own.
Even those "'passing' shocks aren't proving to be short-lived, or one-off events," but are producing more persistent price pressures than at first expected, Barkin said.
"It is tempting to try to blame high inflation on a handful of categories with particularly high exposure to the Middle East conflict or to tariffs," he said. But much of the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index is increasing at greater than a 3% annual rate.
"I am hearing momentum outside of data centers, too. The defense sector is hot. Manufacturing contacts are starting to sound more upbeat. Bankers tell us pipelines are healthy," Barkin said.
(Reporting by Howard Schneider; Editing by Paul Simao)

items.title: Taiwan Minister Says He Was Not ‘Belittled’ on Rare Trip to China
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: By Yi-Chin Lee and Ann Wang A Taiwanese minister returned from a rare trip to China on Tuesday, saying he was well treated and not “belittled” while attending a regional APEC meeting, though he was still happy to be home. Labor Minister Hung Sun-han …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
By Yi-Chin Lee and Ann Wang

A Taiwanese minister returned from a rare trip to China on Tuesday, saying he was well treated and not “belittled” while attending a regional APEC meeting, though he was still happy to be home.

Labor Minister Hung Sun-han was the first minister in President Lai Ching-te’s government to visit China as Beijing has ramped up military and political pressure against Taipei.

The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation group is one of the few international bodies that Chinese-claimed Taiwan belongs to.

Speaking at Taiwan’s main international airport, Taoyuan, on arrival, Hung said China fulfilled its obligations as host nation by granting Taiwan the same rights of equal treatment and dignity as any other APEC member.

“So through our efforts, we actually did not encounter any situation of being belittled in our conference participation,” he added, having been in China since Sunday for a meeting about human resources.

China’s Taiwan Affairs Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Taiwan takes part in APEC under the name “Chinese Taipei”, which it also uses for the Olympics.

Hung said he did not use, and had not applied for, a Taiwan compatriot permit, a Chinese government document most Taiwanese use to travel to China, instead entering with a formal invitation letter to the meeting.

China has rejected repeated offers of talks by Lai, saying he is a “separatist”, and its military operates around Taiwan on an almost daily basis. Lai says only Taiwan’s people can decide their future.

Asked how he felt about being the first senior official to go to China in a decade since Lai, or his predecessor Tsai Ing-wen, took office, Hung said: “It’s really more relaxing to return to Taiwan”.

Lower-level Taiwanese officials have attended other APEC events in China, whose government views Taiwan as a Chinese province and not a country.

Taiwan has yet to announce who will attend the November APEC leaders’ summit in Shenzhen, though its presidents never go.

items.title: Trump vows 'unmatched military might' as he rallies regional anti-cartel allies
items.author: Simon Lewis
items.creator: Simon Lewis
items.summary: President Donald Trump vowed on Tuesday to reassert US dominance in the Western Hemisphere and to use "unmatched military might" against threats in the region as he gathered allies behind an expanding campaign against drug cartels.
items.body:
President Donald Trump vowed on Tuesday to reassert US dominance in the Western Hemisphere and to use "unmatched military might" against threats in the region as he gathered allies behind an expanding campaign against drug cartels.
Speaking to world leaders at the UN General Assembly, Trump cast drug cartels as "the ISIS of the Western Hemisphere" and urged a tougher response to transnational crime.
He spoke ahead of a meeting later on Tuesday with leaders and foreign ministers from the Shield of the Americas, an anti-cartel coalition launched by his administration.
The US raid that captured Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro and a subsequent oil deal with the interim government underscored the US willingness to act in the region, he said.
“Our actions in Venezuela are proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere, and if necessary, we will use our unmatched military might to secure the vital national interests of the United States.”
Trump's National Security Strategy late last year set out plans for a revamped Monroe Doctrine, the 19th-century policy asserting US primacy across the Americas that critics have long associated with decades of American intervention. Trump himself has taken to calling it the "Donroe Doctrine," a play on his own name, after the phrase gained currency in conservative media.
SHIELD OF THE AMERICAS Trump is set to join a meeting of leaders and foreign ministers from the Shield of the Americas, a coalition against drug cartels, as he seeks to rally Latin American nations behind a more aggressive approach that has included US military strikes on drug boats since last fall and greater cooperation with Latin American countries.
Trump launched the group in March, gathering more than a dozen regional leaders in Florida.
The coalition includes governments closely aligned with Trump, including countries like Argentina, Ecuador and El Salvador whose leaders Trump has either praised or endorsed as candidates. Colombia and Peru joined after a Trump-aligned presidents took power in recent months.
Brazil and Mexico are among the countries that have not joined.
Since returning to power early last year, Trump has designated drug cartels as foreign terrorist organizations and launched dozens of deadly strikes on boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific that US officials say are carrying narcotics bound for the US. Rights groups have said the strikes, which have killed more than 220 people, amount to extrajudicial killings.
"For decades, other administrations allowed much of this region to be dominated by vicious gangs and bloodthirsty drug cartels, destabilized by uncontrolled migration, and infiltrated by hostile foreign adversaries - foreign sick, demented adversaries - but not anymore," Trump told the UN, adding that he was "reasserting American power" to make the region safer by taking out cartels.
“Like ISIS, they should be killed, exiled or detained as enemy combatants without the possibility of release,” Trump said, “which is what we're doing.”
Trump also touted his administration’s pressure campaign on Communist-run Cuba, accused its leaders of seeding “subversive and radical” left-wing groups in the United States, and said Secretary of State Marco Rubio was “deep into negotiations with Cuba.”
Drug cartels controlling territory in US neighbor Mexico were “unacceptable,” he said, insisting that the government there “must reclaim control of its soil from the enemies of humanity.”

items.title: Anthropic apresenta Claude Opus 5.5
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A Anthropic lançou nesta terça-feira o Claude Opus 5.5, que definiu como seu modelo de inteligência artificial mais poderoso até o momento, oferecendo um desempenho que, segundo a empresa, rivaliza com o de seu sistema de ponta a um preço significativamente mais baixo.
items.body:
A Anthropic lançou nesta terça-feira o Claude Opus 5.5, que definiu como seu modelo de inteligência artificial mais poderoso até o momento, oferecendo um desempenho que, segundo a empresa, rivaliza com o de seu sistema de ponta a um preço significativamente mais baixo.
A empresa afirmou que o Opus 5.5 apresenta desempenho equivalente ao do modelo Claude Fable 5.1 na maioria das tarefas, ao mesmo tempo em que custa 40% menos para ser executado em cargas de trabalho típicas do que seu antecessor, o Claude Opus 5.
O modelo é mais rápido, mais barato e escreve com mais clareza do que as versões anteriores, afirmou a Anthropic, ao mesmo tempo em que supera seus modelos mais recentes em testes internos de segurança e apresenta 85% menos probabilidade de tentar contornar os limites estabelecidos do que o Opus 5 ou o Mythos 5.1.
O modelo custa US$4 por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$20 por milhão de tokens de saída, 20% a menos que o Opus 5.
(Por Anhata Rooprai)

items.title: Motivated De Bruyne wants to keep playing for Belgium
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Belgium midfielder Kevin De Bruyne will continue to play international football as long as he remains motivated, saying he had not considered quitting the team after the World Cup despite being the last of the country's golden generation.
items.body:
Belgium midfielder Kevin De Bruyne will continue to play international football as long as he remains motivated, saying he had not considered quitting the team after the World Cup despite being the last of the country's golden generation.
De Bruyne, 35, has won 124 caps since his debut as a teenager in 2010 under Georges Leekens and is lined up to add more appearances as Belgium now have Mark van Bommel in charge.
The new era begins against Italy in Rome on Friday, followed by Nations League clashes with France (twice) and Turkey over the next three weeks.
In recent weeks, De Bruyne has seen long-time colleague Axel Witsel retire and goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois sit out the Nations League but told reporters on Tuesday he had never considered quitting the national team.
"No, that was never an issue for me," he said. "The coach did ask me what I wanted to do. My feeling after the World Cup was that I had enjoyed myself. A lot of players also asked me to stay.
"I also felt physically good and still wanted to play. That's the most important motivation. As long as I still have that motivation, why wouldn't I continue?"
DE BRUYNE IMPRESSED WITH NEW COACH De Bruyne did not feel the need for an arrangement like Courtois' to temporarily sit out the Nations League.
"There will come a day when I say that I don't need to do it anymore, but that's not something that is on my mind at the moment.
"I do think these will be my final two years," but then, hesitating, added: "Never say never. At the moment I feel good, so we'll see."
De Bruyne said he was impressed with new coach Van Bommel. "A typical Dutchman, very direct in his dealings. I like that, just someone who says things as they are.
"We now have to try to make a good start, and after four matches we'll know what we can achieve," added the Napoli midfielder.
"I think my level is pretty good. I'm quite satisfied with the way I'm playing. I was surprised by how fit I was when I returned in August and by how sharp I feel.
"I've also now played three matches in a row for 90 minutes. If I can continue like this, that's great for me. It's very positive. My level compared with 10 years ago? There's a difference, but that's normal too," De Bruyne said.

items.title: Saudi Arabia denies buying oil tankers after Iraq blames it for higher shipping costs
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Saudi Arabia on Tuesday denied an Iraqi claim that it had bought 25 oil tankers, saying the information was inaccurate, after Iraq linked the alleged purchases to a sharp increase in the cost of shipping its crude.
items.body:
Saudi Arabia on Tuesday denied an Iraqi claim that it had bought 25 oil tankers, saying the information was inaccurate, after Iraq linked the alleged purchases to a sharp increase in the cost of shipping its crude.
Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Mohammed told a parliamentary session that Saudi Arabia had bought 25 oil tankers worth an estimated $4.5 billion and said the purchases were behind a steep rise in the cost of transporting Iraqi oil. His remarks were published by an Iraqi media outlet on Facebook on Monday.
Mohammed said transport costs had risen from $26 per barrel to $37 per barrel.
Saudi Arabia and Iraq are the two largest oil producers in the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries. A public disagreement between their energy ministers is rare.
In a statement, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said it had not purchased the tankers and attributed the rise in oil transport costs to several factors, including regional military conflict and disruption to navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.
It said those conditions had pushed shipping costs in the region to "exceptional levels".
The dispute comes as attacks on Saudi cities, energy infrastructure and shipping continue, raising concerns about global oil supplies and threatening the Red Sea, a key alternative export route for Gulf producers while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted.
Iraq has been among the countries most affected by the closure of the strategic waterway. Traffic through the strait remains well below pre-conflict levels and vessels continue to face attacks in the area.

items.title: Trump at UN: Threats, diplomacy and 'super intelligence'
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: President Donald Trump used his address to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday to defend the US-Israeli campaign against Iran while laying out his foreign policy priorities. Here are the major issues he addressed in a 37-minute speech:
items.body:
President Donald Trump used his address to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday to defend the US-Israeli campaign against Iran while laying out his foreign policy priorities. Here are the major issues he addressed in a 37-minute speech:
* IRAN. He warned he could [USN:L1N45D0Z2 TEXT:"annihilate Iran"] without a peace deal and predicted one would be reached after US midterm elections on November 3 when the makeup of Congress will be decided.
* UKRAINE. About Russia's war in Ukraine, he said, "We're working very closely with the leaders of Russia and Ukraine, and we will get that one done," adding, "It's going to happen, I think, more quickly than people understand."
* ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE. He said the US government would use the term "super intelligence" instead of artificial intelligence and repeated his view that AI safety warnings are a hoax. "We're leading now over China by a lot and everyone else," he said. "I'm not going to stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution." He said US law enforcement agencies would rein in the sector if needed.
* INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL COURT. He urged member nations of the International Criminal Court to withdraw – he used the word "resign" – and condemned what he called an "out of control institution" and "an evil group of people." He said the US would not allow military service members to be subject to what he called show trials by an anti-American tribunal.
* DRUG WARS. He said he was "reasserting American power" to make the region safer by taking out cartels, which the US has designated terrorist organizations. “Like ISIS, they should be killed, exiled or detained as enemy combatants without the possibility of release,” Trump said, “which is what we're doing.”
* VENEZUELA. He characterized his administration's actions in Venezuela as a great victory and a potential warning to others. "Our actions in Venezuela are proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere, and if necessary, we will use our unmatched military might to secure the vital national interests of the United States," he said.
* CUBA. He called Cuba a failed state and, touting greater US involvement in the region, adding: "Communism will never be coming to America, but freedom will be coming to Cuba." Members of the Cuban UN delegation walked out.
* MEXICO. He called Mexico an epicenter of regional drug cartel violence.
* THE UN ITSELF. He touted what he described as sweeping UN reforms under his administration, including budget cuts and staff reductions, while attacking international organizations and efforts to create global taxes. "The United Nations has great, great potential. I've said that for many years. But it must stop imposing the far-left agenda of globalist bureaucrats who nobody ever elected," he said.

items.title: Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Egypt affirm Riyadh's right to defend itself
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The foreign ministers of Turkey, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan said in a joint statement on Tuesday that they affirmed Riyadh's right to defend itself in line with international law and stressed the need to maintain safety of navigation in the region, amid escalating attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis.
items.body:
The foreign ministers of Turkey, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan said in a joint statement on Tuesday that they affirmed Riyadh's right to defend itself in line with international law and stressed the need to maintain safety of navigation in the region, amid escalating attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis.
Following a meeting on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York, the ministers also expressed deep concern over the ongoing conflicts in the region, saying dialogue and diplomacy were the only pat to a sustainable solution. They also voiced their support for Yemen's government in its efforts to achieve stability and peace.

items.title: El Real Madrid pide un nuevo presidente de LaLiga española tras las declaraciones de Tebas
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El Real Madrid quiere un nuevo presidente de LaLiga española a raíz de lo que calificó como comentarios "intolerables" por parte del actual presidente, Javier Tebas, quien afirmó este martes que las acusaciones de parcialidad arbitral contra el club pertenecen a "otra galaxia".
items.body:
El Real Madrid quiere un nuevo presidente de LaLiga española a raíz de lo que calificó como comentarios "intolerables" por parte del actual presidente, Javier Tebas, quien afirmó este martes que las acusaciones de parcialidad arbitral contra el club pertenecen a "otra galaxia".
Tras caer por 2-1 ante el Atlético de Madrid el domingo, el Real Madrid tituló la crónica del partido en su página web: "Un pésimo arbitraje decide el derbi".
El Real Madrid se mostró furioso porque el defensa argentino del Atlético Cristian "Cuti" Romero no fuera expulsado por un pisotón en el muslo a Jude Bellingham y también se quejó de una entrada de Lee Kang-in sobre Federico Valverde.
El entrenador del Real Madrid, José Mourinho, dirigió duras críticas al árbitro Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias y a quienes lo designaron. El técnico portugués afirmó que su equipo puede ganar aún el título "si nos dejan competir en igualdad de circunstancias con todos".
El Real Madrid ocupa actualmente el cuarto puesto, a seis puntos del vigente campeón, el Fútbol Club Barcelona, después de siete jornadas.
Tebas había declarado el lunes que el discurso que está promoviendo el Real Madrid es una cortina de humo para encubrir las deficiencias en el terreno de juego.
"Sostener que los árbitros están dirigidos contra el Real Madrid es vivir en otra galaxia", declaró Tebas en las redes sociales. "Ese relato sirve de coartada para tapar otras carencias que se ven a simple vista en estos primeros partidos de la temporada. Es más cómodo señalar una conspiración que explicar lo que ocurre en el césped".
El Real Madrid respondió con un comunicado en su página web en el que condenó las palabras de Tebas y afirmó que LaLiga necesita un nuevo liderazgo.
"Nuestro club considera intolerable que el presidente de LaLiga utilice su posición institucional para seguir descalificando y atacando al Real Madrid de la manera que lo hace en cada una de sus intervenciones", indicó el comunicado.
"A tenor de este comportamiento inadecuado y sostenido en el tiempo, entendemos que la competición profesional de fútbol en España necesita con urgencia un dirigente capaz de administrarla y de desarrollar todo su potencial con el deber elemental de la neutralidad", agregó.
Reuters solicitó a LaLiga que se pronuncie al respecto. Tebas, que se autoproclama aficionado del Real Madrid, lleva al frente de LaLiga desde 2013. En diciembre de 2023 se presentó sin oposición a un cuarto mandato y su cargo actual se extiende hasta 2027.
Durante su presidencia, Tebas se ha pronunciado con frecuencia sobre los desacuerdos con el Real Madrid, mientras que LaLiga y el club también se han enfrentado en los tribunales en los últimos años.

items.summary: Um caça F-16 destacado na base aérea norte-americana de Spangdahlem, no oeste da Alemanha, sofreu um acidente nesta terça-feira, informaram militares dos EUA, acrescentando que um piloto conseguiu se ejetar em segurança e estava recebendo atendimento médico.
items.body:
Um caça F-16 destacado na base aérea norte-americana de Spangdahlem, no oeste da Alemanha, sofreu um acidente nesta terça-feira, informaram militares dos EUA, acrescentando que um piloto conseguiu se ejetar em segurança e estava recebendo atendimento médico.
A causa do incidente está sendo investigada, informaram as forças norte-americanas em um comunicado, com equipes de emergência no local do acidente.
A autoridade de controle de tráfego aéreo da Alemanha, em comunicado separado, informou que um total de quatro F-16s participavam de um exercício de treinamento.
“Dois ainda estavam na área de treinamento, enquanto dois estavam retornando à Base Aérea de Spangdahlem. Acredita-se que um desses dois jatos tenha caído durante a aproximação”, afirmou, acrescentando que os demais F-16s haviam pousado na base da Força Aérea dos EUA em Ramstein.

items.title: Turkey's Erdogan urges UN reform, wider recognition of Palestinian state
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan told the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday the U.N had become unable to fulfill its duty of preserving peace and called for reform of the Security Council.
items.body:
Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan told the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday the U.N had become unable to fulfill its duty of preserving peace and called for reform of the Security Council.
Erdogan has for years called for a more comprehensive and inclusive structure at the Security Council.
"Let's recognise that a system in which the will of more than 190 countries is subject to the whims of five countries is neither fair nor capable of fully establishing trust," he said.
"The United Nations, established 81 years ago to maintain peace and security, has become unable to fulfil this mission, or rather it has been made unable to do so," he added.
Erdogan also condemned the situation in Gaza, saying "no one who holds humanity, compassion and mercy in their heart, with a sense of justice and conscience can turn a blind eye" to what was happening there.
"(Palestinian President) Mahmoud Abbas, has been unable to take his place in this hall for two consecutive years. This injustice against our Palestinian brothers and sisters wounds the consciences," Erdogan said.
He urged countries that do not recognise a Palestinian state to review their position and for all nations to increase pressure on Israel to end the war in Gaza, which he called "our time's most inhumane, most embarrassing concentration camp".
NATO member Turkey has been one of the most vocal critics of Israel and its war on Gaza, saying its attacks amounted to genocide. It has repeatedly urged for international measures against Israel. Israel denies accusations of genocide.

[２２日 ロイター] - 米軍は２２日、ドイツ西部のシュパングダーレム米空軍基地所属のＦ１６戦闘機１機が墜落したと発表した。操縦士１人は無事脱出し、治療を受けている。

items.title: France/Carburant L'aide "aux gros rouleurs" reconduite et élargie
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le gouvernement français a annoncé mardi un élargissement de l'aide aux automobilistes les plus dépendants de leur véhicule, dans le cadre d'un nouveau train de mesures destiné à amortir l'impact de la flambée des prix des carburants provoquée par les perturbations de l'approvisionnement mondial en pétrole.
items.body:
Le gouvernement français a annoncé mardi un élargissement de l'aide aux automobilistes les plus dépendants de leur véhicule, dans le cadre d'un nouveau train de mesures destiné à amortir l'impact de la flambée des prix des carburants provoquée par les perturbations de l'approvisionnement mondial en pétrole.
"L'essence est à son prix le plus haut depuis le début du conflit" et "a désormais dépassé son précédent pic", a constaté en préambule le ministre de l'Économie Roland Lescure, en présentant une réponse gouvernementale "amplifiée" et "élargie" d'un montant estimé à 450 millions d'euros.
L'aide de 100 euros destinée aux "grands rouleurs" sera renouvelée et étendue à 5,5 millions de Français, contre trois millions lors du précédent dispositif, pour les mois d'octobre, novembre et décembre, a annoncé la porte-parole du gouvernement Maud Brégeon.
"Pour ces bénéficiaires, cette aide représentera l'équivalent de 0,40 euro par litre de carburant" et concernera désormais des revenus allant jusqu'à 2.035 euros nets par mois pour une personne seule, a-t-elle précisé, et jusqu'à 6.104 euros pour un couple avec enfants.
"La crise dure. Une usure réelle se fait sentir", a ajouté Maud Brégeon, jugeant que l'impact croissant sur le pouvoir d'achat "justifie cet élargissement et ce renouvellement" de l'aide.
Le gouvernement maintiendra par ailleurs le chèque énergie dans son projet de budget pour 2027 et en avancera le versement à janvier, contre avril habituellement.
Le ministre de l'Action et des comptes publics, David Amiel, a rejeté les accusations selon lesquelles l'État bénéficierait d'une hausse de ses recettes avec l'augmentation des prix à la pompe.
"Il n'y a pas eu, il n'y a pas et il n'y aura pas de cagnotte", a-t-il dit, évoquant une perte de recettes fiscales de 407 millions d'euros liée aux carburants.
Le gouvernement proposera dans le budget 2027 un mécanisme prévoyant que tout éventuel surplus de recettes lié à la fiscalité des carburants soit "immédiatement restitué aux Français sous la forme d'aides supplémentaires".
Cette règle, a-t-il dit, s'inscrit dans une stratégie d'aides "temporaires, ciblées et financées" afin d'éviter de "promettre d'une main pour aller ensuite reprendre de l'autre".
Ces annonces interviennent après que le président Emmanuel Macron [USN:L8N45E0DB TEXT:"s'est tourné vendredi vers la Commission européenne"] afin qu'elle prenne des mesures visant à améliorer l'offre en carburants.

items.title: DeepSeek deve fazer apresentação ao Conselho de Segurança da ONU sobre IA
items.author: Laurie Chen
items.creator: Laurie Chen
items.summary: A startup chinesa de inteligência artificial DeepSeek estará entre as empresas que farão uma apresentação ao Conselho de Segurança das Nações Unidas nesta semana sobre os riscos representados pela inteligência artificial, disseram duas fontes a par do assunto.
items.body:
A startup chinesa de inteligência artificial DeepSeek estará entre as empresas que farão uma apresentação ao Conselho de Segurança das Nações Unidas nesta semana sobre os riscos representados pela inteligência artificial, disseram duas fontes a par do assunto.
O Conselho de Segurança, composto por 15 membros, deve se reunir na quarta-feira para discutir IA e segurança internacional, semanas depois que vários líderes do setor de IA pediram uma desaceleração coordenada no desenvolvimento da tecnologia, alertando que ela pode em breve se aperfeiçoar por conta própria e escapar do controle humano.
O presidente-executivo da OpenAI, Sam Altman, planeja fazer uma apresentação na reunião, na qual diplomatas também esperam a participação de representantes de alto escalão da Anthropic, informou a Reuters na semana passada.
A DeepSeek e outras empresas chinesas de IA, incluindo Moonshot, foram convidadas a fazerem apresentações, disse uma das fontes.
O fundador da DeepSeek, Liang Wenfeng, não planeja comparecer, disse a fonte, alertando que os planos ainda são provisórios e podem mudar no último minuto.
DeepSeek e Moonshot não comentaram o assunto.
O Conselho de Segurança da ONU, encarregado de manter a paz e a segurança internacionais, reuniu-se pela primeira vez para discutir os riscos da inteligência artificial em 2023. Na ocasião, a China alertou que a tecnologia não deveria se tornar um “cavalo fora de controle”, e os Estados Unidos defenderam que ela não deve ser usada para censurar ou reprimir as pessoas.
O secretário-geral da ONU, António Guterres, alertou os líderes mundiais na semana passada que o rápido avanço da IA representa riscos que não podem ser ignorados, colocando-o em desacordo com o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, que argumentou que as salvaguardas existentes são suficientes e que a China se beneficiará das dúvidas lançadas sobre o desenvolvimento da IA.
A mídia estatal chinesa rejeitou os apelos por uma desaceleração no desenvolvimento da IA, classificando-os como provenientes de um “manual da Guerra Fria”, com o objetivo de preservar o domínio de Washington em tecnologia de ponta e excluir Pequim do sistema global de governança da IA.
Ao contrário dos líderes de empresas pioneiras dos EUA, como OpenAI e Anthropic, os chefes das principais empresas chinesas de desenvolvimento de modelos de IA raramente expressam publicamente a possibilidade de que sistemas de IA cada vez mais capazes possam enganar os seres humanos, escapar ao controle ou causar danos catastróficos.
Eles também permaneceram em grande parte em silêncio sobre esses riscos desde que o debate se intensificou nos EUA neste mês.
Autoridades de alto escalão dos EUA e da China concordaram em realizar novas negociações sobre segurança em IA, afirmou o secretário do Tesouro dos EUA, Scott Bessent, na segunda-feira, após uma reunião realizada antes das conversas programadas entre Trump e o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, no final desta semana, em Washington.

items.title: Swiss finance minister and UBS boss face off ahead of capital decision
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Swiss Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter and UBS CEO Sergio Ermotti on Tuesday defended their opposing views on new Swiss capital rules in a last round of appeals before a key parliamentary decision on Wednesday.
items.body:
Swiss Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter and UBS (UBSG.S) CEO Sergio Ermotti on Tuesday defended their opposing views on new Swiss capital rules in a last round of appeals before a key parliamentary decision on Wednesday.
Keller-Sutter, who oversaw the UBS takeover of Credit Suisse after the latter collapsed in 2023, said backing foreign units with 100% Common Equity Tier 1 capital was the best way to protect taxpayers.
Her proposal, which has won backing from the Swiss National Bank, would make shareholders rather than taxpayer liable for losses, she told an event in Zurich.
Another proposal under consideration in parliament's upper chamber, which seeks 90% CET1 backing of foreign units is close to the government's submission, Keller-Sutter added.
Ermotti has rejected both [USN:L8N45E0C2 TEXT:"outcomes"] as unacceptable and said the debate should acknowledge that UBS is not only a risk for Switzerland but also a benefit to its economy.
"We are very concerned that this would make us uncompetitive and ultimately call into question the sustainability of the business model," he told the same audience in Zurich.
"Over the coming weeks and months, we will shape the future of the financial center for the next 10 to 20 years," Ermotti added.
Following the decision in the upper house, the capital rules bill will move to the lower house of parliament, with a final decision expected at the end of this year at the earliest, and more likely in 2027.

items.title: Anthropic unveils Claude Opus 5.5
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Anthropic on Tuesday released Claude Opus 5.5, which it called its most powerful AI model to date, offering performance it said rivals its top-tier system at a significantly lower price.
items.body:
Anthropic on Tuesday released Claude Opus 5.5, which it called its most powerful AI model to date, offering performance it said rivals its top-tier system at a significantly lower price.
The company said Opus 5.5 performs on par with its Claude Fable 5.1 model on most tasks while costing 40% less to run on typical workloads than its predecessor, [USN:L6N43P1GI TEXT:"Claude Opus 5"].
The model is faster, cheaper and writes more clearly than earlier versions, Anthropic said, while outperforming its recent models on internal safety tests, and being 85% less likely than Opus 5 or Mythos 5.1 to attempt to bypass its prescribed boundaries.
The model is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, 20% below Opus 5.
