items.title: Trump administration asks US Supreme Court to allow detention of pro-Palestinian scholar
items.author: Nate Raymond
items.creator: Nate Raymond
items.summary: President Donald Trump's administration has asked the US Supreme Court to overturn a decision that led to the release of a Georgetown University scholar who had advocated for Palestinian rights and opposed Israel's war in Gaza.
items.body:
President Donald Trump's administration has asked the US Supreme Court to overturn a decision that led to the release of a Georgetown University scholar who had advocated for Palestinian rights and opposed Israel's war in Gaza.
The Department of Justice on Monday asked the high court to consider whether federal immigration law barred a lower-court judge from ordering Badar Khan Suri released, after hearing his claims that his detention violated his due process and free speech rights under the US Constitution.
The Indian citizen had been [USN:L4N3SY1DC TEXT:"arrested"] by immigration authorities in March 2025 as the Trump administration pursued a campaign to detain and deport foreign nationals who had engaged in pro-Palestinian activism on their college campuses.
He was brought to Texas after his detention, and freed in May 2025 on the orders of a district court judge, on the grounds that he was likely to succeed in proving his arrest was in retaliation for his constitutionally protected speech. The Trump administration has argued that the judge should not have interfered in the case.
A 2-1 panel of the Richmond, Virginia-based 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals [USN:L1N43P1HF TEXT:"in July ruled"] in Suri's case that nothing prevented a judge from hearing a challenge to someone's allegedly unconstitutional detention, even if it related to deportation proceedings pending before the immigration courts.
Solicitor General D. John Sauer in Monday's petition argued that the 4th Circuit's ruling was wrong and risked disrupting immigration enforcement nationwide by giving detainees a means to challenge their deportations outside of immigration court.
"That is all practically disastrous," he wrote.
He noted that a different appeals court had reached the opposite conclusion earlier this year when it overturned a ruling that had led to the release of another pro-Palestinian activist, [USN:L1N41Z0RU TEXT:"Mahmoud Khalil"], who had attended Columbia University.
Khalil's lawyers have said they plan to appeal that decision to the Supreme Court, and Sauer in Monday's filing argued that the justices should take up that case as well as Suri's to ensure that the issue can be resolved once and for all.
Suri's lawyers did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Suri is a postdoctoral fellow at Georgetown's Alwaleed Bin Talal Center for Muslim-Christian Understanding, part of the Jesuit university's School of Foreign Service. At the time of his arrest, he had resided in Virginia with his wife, a US citizen.

Sept 22 : Palo Alto Networks said on Tuesday it would launch a new cybersecurity service for businesses, using advanced AI models from Anthropic and OpenAI to help identify security vulnerabilities across corporate systems.
Hackers are increasingly using AI to find and exploit weaknesses in corporate networks, prompting cybersecurity firms to build defenses that can detect and respond to threats more quickly.
The service, called Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense, will use cyber-focused AI models including Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Cyber, along with open-weight models, the company said.
The offering is designed to continuously test web applications, application programming interfaces and cloud infrastructure, helping customers identify vulnerabilities and possible attack paths as their digital environments change.

items.author: CNA

Netanyahu says will 'tell the truth' on Israel's actions at United Nations

Netanyahu is slated to speak at the UN's General Assembly on Thursday.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks during a toast-raising event hosted by his Likud party in Tel Aviv, Israel, on Sep 17, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Amir Cohen)

JERUSALEM: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday (Sep 22) he would use his speech at the United Nations this week to defend Israel's military actions against the Palestinians, while accusing New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani of supporting Hamas.
Netanyahu's comments were in response to remarks by the New York mayor, who told CNN on Monday that Netanyahu was a "war criminal and an architect of a horrific genocide of the Palestinian people".
Netanyahu is slated to speak at the UN's General Assembly on Thursday.
"I'm coming to the UN," Netanyahu said in a brief video statement. "I'm going to tell the truth about our heroic soldiers, and I'm going to tell the truth about you (Mamdani)."

Mamdani had previously said he would arrest Netanyahu, but acknowledged he did not have the power to do so.
"Shame on you, Mr Mamdani," Netanyahu said. "Shame on you for supporting the Hamas terrorist monsters who butchered our people. Shame on you for inciting riots against New York Jews."
Some Republican opponents have called Mamdani antisemitic, citing his pro-Palestinian advocacy and criticism of Israel's military action in Gaza.
Mamdani has condemned antisemitism. He says his criticism of Israel is wrongly conflated with antisemitism.

Related:

UN investigators say Israel committing genocide in Gaza

UN demands Israel prevent 'genocide' in Gaza

The Hamas raid on Israel on Oct 7, 2023, killed about 1,200 people, while another 251 were kidnapped, Israeli authorities have said.
Israel responded with an air and ground assault it says was aimed at dismantling Hamas' military and governing capabilities. More than 73,000 Palestinians have been killed, according to Gaza health officials, a toll that does not distinguish between fighters and non-combatants.
Israel has denied it has perpetrated a genocide against Palestinians in Gaza, saying it was fighting Hamas militants and accusing the group of hiding behind civilians.
Last week, Netanyahu spokesman Doron Spielman told Reuters that Netanyahu has already spoken to the United Nations more than any other world leader, "and he's going to use that platform to address the truth in a forum of countries that are often buying a false narrative about Israel".
"It's one of the most important stages for the Prime Minister of Israel to stand on and present the truth to the world. That's our goal. He's not intimidated by anybody. He's not intimidated by Mayor Mamdani," he said.

Source: Reuters/rk

items.title: Can the UN remain relevant?
items.author: Sharon Kimathi
items.creator: Sharon Kimathi
items.summary: Today's newsletter focuses on the environment and governance themes that will be addressed at the 2026 UN General Assembly, which takes place against a backdrop of rising temperatures, geopolitical tension over minerals and the rise of AI.
items.body:
Today's newsletter focuses on the environment and governance themes that will be addressed at the 2026 UN General Assembly, which takes place against a backdrop of rising temperatures, geopolitical tension over minerals and the rise of AI.
US President Donald Trump is expected to kick it off with a speech. Last year, he told delegates that some countries were "going to hell" for, among other things, climate policy and mass migration.[USN:L1N45D0Z2 TEXT:" Click here"] for the latest on who he is meeting.
This year’s General Assembly faces an existential debate over the UN’s relevance, with the theme: "Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all”.
UN RELEVANCE IN ADDRESSING CRISES The UN is struggling to remain relevant as it faces attacks from Trump , whose administration has cut US contributions and withdrawn from dozens of UN bodies.
The US avoided losing its vote at the assembly by paying $725 million in contributions to the regular budget last week, but it still owes the UN more than $1 billion and makes ongoing demands for cuts and reforms.
Additionally, [USN:L4N45906F TEXT:"China’s President Xi Jinping"], who last addressed the meeting via video in 2021, will skip New York in favour of talks with Trump in Washington on Thursday, adding to the debate about the UN's relevance in addressing global crises.
There are also questions about the leadership of the 80-year-old organization as Secretary-General Antonio Guterres completes his term at the end of 2026, with no clear frontrunner in the[USN:L6N3W20WS TEXT:" race"] to replace him.
Guterres told reporters ahead of the meeting that the need for stronger oversight would be a major focus of his talks with global leaders gathered in New York.
GREENLAND AND EXCEEDING 1.5 DEGREES CELSIUS Trump is also due to meet with leaders of [USN:L6N45E05Y TEXT:"Greenland and Denmark"] on Tuesday to sign a deal that will allow a[USN:L1N45D0X6 TEXT:" larger US military presence"] on Greenland and could end[USN:L8N4051Z5 TEXT:" a standoff"] over the strategically located and mineral-rich island.
Greenland, a former colony and now a semi-autonomous territory of the[USN:L1N3O40E8 TEXT:" Kingdom of Denmark"], sits between the Arctic and North America.
Climate change will also be on the agenda as the world struggles to limit warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. World leaders agreed to limit warming in the 2015 Paris climate agreement and heads of smaller island nations and other states most affected by climate change are expected to again urge action.
August was the first month since November 2025 in which the world's average temperature[USN:L6N4510XR TEXT:" exceeded"] 1.5 C above pre-industrial levels.
TALKING POINTS Tesla racism lawsuit: A lawsuit by the California Civil Rights Department, a state agency, accusing Tesla of allowing rampant race discrimination at its flagship assembly plant began trial this week and is scheduled to run until October 30. In the lawsuit filed in 2022, the agency claims Black workers at Tesla's Fremont, California, plant were subjected to pervasive harassment by other employees, including racial slurs and graffiti, and Tesla failed to prevent or stop it. Tesla has denied wrongdoing. [USN:L1N45A0KF TEXT:"Click here"] to learn more about the suit.
Taxes and inequality: A ballot initiative on November 3 will ask Californians whether to impose a one-time 5% tax on the state's billionaires . The proposition is far from certain to pass, political analysts say, amid a debate that has raised questions about income inequality and California’s future business prospects.
Cuba crisis: [USN:S0N44A00N TEXT:"Cuba's electrical grid"] suffered a total collapse at the weekend, leaving millions without power amid a US pressure campaign that has largely blocked oil from reaching the Caribbean's largest island. The latest of at least six partial or total grid collapses since January hardly registered in a country accustomed to long hours, or even days, without power.
Bangladesh factory cooling: Brands should share the cost burden when investing in cooling systems to reduce heat stress for garment factory workers, researchers at Cornell University's Global Labor Institute said in a report, as climate change poses growing risks to apparel production hubs. [USN:L6N4560U5 TEXT:"Click here"] for the full Reuters insight.
New Zealand carbon credits: For almost 20 years, New Zealand has pioneered one of the world’s most ambitious tree-planting programs, approving nearly 9,000 square kilometers of carbon-credit forest. That’s about 11 times the land area of New York City. Yet the boom in carbon forestry, and tradable carbon credits, has also driven competition for sheep and beef farming land. Click here for the full Reuters special deep-dive story.
IN CONVERSATION Kaysie Brown, associate director of climate diplomacy and geopolitics at climate change think tank E3G, shares her thoughts on the UN General Assembly:
"As the majority of the world's leaders come together in New York, this is the moment to stand fast on cooperation in a fragmenting world.
“The crises on their agenda, from energy shocks from ongoing conflict in the Middle East and Ukraine to record heat, wildfires and a looming El Niño, are not reasons to set climate aside; they are the reason to act on it, faster and together.”
“In Secretary-General Guterres's final year, leaders must show their resolve in building on the economic opportunities that clean energy and climate action affords, and to tackle challenges jointly to build the resilience their people need."
ESG SPOTLIGHT Away from the debate at the UN, we highlight a story about rescuing puppies.
[USN:L8N4590QN TEXT:"Click here"] to read about a pilot programme run by German animal welfare association Tierhilfe Hoffnung that aims to provide a better alternative to Romania’s policy of culling unwanted animals.
Think your friend or colleague should know about us? Forward this newsletter to them. They can also subscribe here .

Sept 22 : Bundesliga basement side Borussia Moenchengladbach appointed Alexander Blessin as manager on Tuesday after they started the season with four straight league defeats.
Gladbach sacked Eugen Polanski on September 13 and brought in Jan-Moritz Lichte on an interim basis but it did not improve their fortunes as they lost 4-3 to Mainz the following weekend.
Blessin has a contract until June 2028.
His last job was a two-year spell at St Pauli that ended in June, having taken over after they were promoted to the Bundesliga under Fabian Huerzeler and kept the club in the top flight for a season before they were relegated last term.

"Blessin will be officially unveiled at a press conference at ista-Borussia-Park at 13:30 CEST on Wednesday, 23rd September, with Head of Sports Rouven Schroeder in attendance," said Gladbach in a statement on their website.
The St Pauli job was Blessin's first as a senior manager in German football, although he spent eight years at RB Leipzig as a youth coach after being brought in by Ralf Rangnick.
Previously, he had spells in Belgium and Italy, taking charge of KV Oostende, Genoa and Union Saint-Gilloise.
Gladbach finished 12th last season, nine points clear of the relegation playoff position. Blessin will have time during the international break to work with his players before they return to action in the Bundesliga on October 11 at FC Cologne.

FAST

Sept 22 : Data startup Snorkel AI has raised $350 million in fresh funding at a $3.5 billion valuation, its CEO Alex Ratner told Reuters, as booming demand from frontier AI labs for increasingly complex training data and simulated environments fuels rapid growth.
Led by Insight Partners and S32, the funding round included participation from existing investors Addition, Greylock and Wells Fargo, the company said. The deal values the company at nearly three times the $1.3 billion valuation achieved when it last raised $100 million in May 2025.
The San Francisco-based company said its annualized revenue run-rate has crossed $350 million, from roughly $20 million a year earlier, driven by the data-as-a-service business it launched in September 2025.
Founded in 2019 by a team of researchers spinning out of the Stanford AI lab, Snorkel AI initially sold software but has shifted toward supplying finished datasets and reinforcement-learning, or RL, environments directly to customers.

Ratner said demand had grown as AI developers moved beyond simpler labeling work and sought harder, higher-stakes data to train and evaluate increasingly capable systems.
Snorkel now offers what it calls an "agentic data development platform" that pairs human experts with thousands of specialized AI models and agents to create and vet data. Experts devise design scenarios, tasks and grading rubrics, while AI automates much of the labor-intensive quality assurance process, Ratner said, as it partners with AI labs to design ways to acquire high-quality datasets.
The business taps a network of tens of thousands of specialists across fields such as coding, law and medicine. Ratner said Snorkel sells the data products they generate rather than charging for human labor, a model that lets it pay experts more generously while preserving margins.
"Our strong view is that 100 per cent of the data that labs will get value out of will have some human input in the foreseeable future," Ratner said. "But 100 per cent of that data will have to use synthetic and automated approaches to keep up with this complexity."
The company says it works with frontier AI labs, hyperscalers, enterprises and the US federal government. Coding data is one of Snorkel's biggest areas of demand.
Venture funding continues to pour into startups supplying frontier AI labs with human-annotated training data, a market transformed after Meta's $14.3 billion purchase of a 49 per cent stake in Scale AI in June 2025. Rivals including Mercor and Surge AI have also attracted investor interest amid strong revenue growth.
Ratner said the fresh capital would be used to hire researchers and engineers, while expanding the company's enterprise and government operations. The startup also plans to support third-party AI model evaluations and push into new industry verticals and data modalities.
While growth remains the priority, the company said it expects to reach profitability this year.
“Data is becoming more rare, more specialized, more difficult to find," said Andy Harrison, partner at S32 who co-led the funding. “If you want to train the most frontier, complex and capable models, now you need superior data."

Source: Reuters

items.title: Amgen's autoimmune drug succeeds in late-stage trial
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Amgen said on Tuesday its experimental drug to treat an autoimmune disease that attacks the body's moisture-producing glands met the main goal of reducing disease activity in a late-stage trial.
items.body:
Amgen (AMGN.O) said on Tuesday its experimental drug to treat an autoimmune disease that attacks the body's moisture-producing glands met the main goal of reducing disease activity in a late-stage trial.
Here are some details:
The drug dazodalibep showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in patients with Sjogren's disease at week 48.
Sjogren's disease can cause extensive dryness of the eyes, mouth and other parts of the body, along with fatigue and chronic pain.
It affects about 1% of the global population and predominantly affects women, according to the National Institutes of Health.
Amgen said most adverse events in the trial were mild to moderate, with few patients discontinuing treatment.
Novartis (NOVN.S) and Johnson & Johnson (JNJ.N) are also developing drugs to treat Sjogren's disease, which has no approved treatments in the US.
Amgen plans to present detailed data from the trial at an upcoming medical meeting. A second late-stage study of dazodalibep in moderate to severe symptomatic Sjogren's disease is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of this year.
(This story has been corrected to say that a separate late-stage trial of the drug is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter, in the last bullet point.)

Sept 22 : Premier League champions Arsenal have agreed an improved contract with manager Mikel Arteta, the BBC reported on Tuesday.
Arteta's deal was due to expire at the end of the season and negotiations over an extension had been ongoing for several months.
Arsenal co-chair Josh Kroenke said in May that securing Arteta's future was the club's priority after the Spaniard guided the North London side to their first league title in 22 years last season.
Reuters has contacted Arsenal for comment.

items.title: Wall Street expects Meta's AI agent to shape into a new revenue engine
items.author: Shashwat Chauhan
items.creator: Shashwat Chauhan
items.summary: Wall Street has turned bullish on Meta Platforms, betting that its new AI agent Muse could open a new revenue stream for the social media giant and reshape the company's AI monetization prospects.
items.body:
Wall Street has turned bullish on Meta Platforms, betting that its new AI agent Muse could open a new revenue stream for the social media giant and reshape the company's AI monetization prospects.
Muse, [USN:L6N45010V TEXT:"launched"] on September 8, is an AI assistant that can send emails, book travel and complete transactions such as selling a car on behalf of a user. The basic version is free, with subscriptions priced at $20 and $100 a month for heavier use.
Since its launch, shares of Meta Platforms (META.O) have surged more than 20%, outpacing the "Magnificent 7" group of US tech companies during the period. Shares have added over $200 billion in market capitalization to touch their highest level in more than seven months as of last close.
Shares were up 1% by noon on Tuesday, after surging more than 11% in the previous session.
"While it is still early, we believe that Muse has the potential to become the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT," J.P.Morgan analysts said in a note, crediting the app's early traction to strong product-market fit, Meta's distribution reach and a free tier that lowers the barrier to trial and repeat use.
The Muse app, available on iOS and Android but only in the US and Canada regions, has clocked 2.8 million downloads in the first 12 days of launch, according to data from Apptopia.
If compared on similar metrics to the first 12 days of OpenAI's ChatGPT, Muse has 1.8 million downloads versus 1.3 million for ChatGPT.
Early reviews suggest "functionality is resonating with users, particularly agent's ability to execute multi-step tasks and workflows with limited user intervention," BofA Global Research analysts said.
Enthusiasm around Muse sparked a Wall Street tech rally on Monday, lifting Meta shares more than 11% and boosting chipmakers, including AMD (AMD.O) and Intel (INTC.O) , with AMD crossing the [USN:L4N45D0ZM TEXT:"$1 trillion"] valuation mark for the first time.
"The market has interpreted Muse as a boon for the already significantly bottlenecked CPU market," said Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading.
Brokerage Jefferies estimated that if Muse could see 1 billion users by end of 2027 and at least 3% transition to a paid version, it could result in $10.8 billion in annualized revenue, as the brokerage raised its price target on Meta's stock to $875.
UBS Global Wealth Management analysts said in a note Meta's Muse provides "early evidence that consumer AI agents could achieve broad adoption, offering new AI monetization opportunities beyond enterprise application."
Of the 64 brokerages that cover Meta's stock, 57 rate it "buy" or higher with a median price target of $760, according to data compiled by LSEG.
"Prior to Muse, investors had completely dismissed the idea that Meta would be able to release a personalized consumer AI agent, favoring (Alphabet) instead," Jefferies analysts led by Brent Thill said.
Meta's Muse follows a series of setbacks with its Llama 4 models last year, including criticism over the benchmark results reported for early versions.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ワシントン　２２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ワシントン　２２日　ロイター］ - ルビオ米国務長官は、トランプ大統領が２２日にニューヨークで行うウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領との会談について、ウクライナとロシアが互いにエネルギーインフラ攻撃を停止することについて協議すると明らかにした。

ルビオ氏はＦＯＸニュースの番組で「ウクライナのインフラが攻撃の標的とされず、ロシアのエネルギー供給も標的とされないエネルギーインフラ停戦は、素晴らしい案だと考えている。理想的な結果だ」と述べた。

また、米国関連の船舶や米国産石油の供給が、「恐らく意図的ではなく」ウクライナの標的になっていることが懸念事項だと指摘。「この問題には対処する必要がある。このような事態を容認することはできない」と述べた。

items.title: 中国、ディープシークとムーンショットを調査－インフォメーション
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国当局は、米アンソロピックが中国企業による同社のAIモデル「Claude（クロード）」を介した機密データの処理を指摘したことを受け、DeepSeek（ディープシーク）とムーンショットAI（月之暗面）のデータセキュリティーをめぐる調査に乗り出した。テクノロジー系ニュースサイトのジ・インフォメーションが事情に詳しい複数の関係者を引用して報じた。関係者の身元は明らかにしていない。

インフォメーションによると、国家インターネット情報弁公室（CAC）は、両社のオフィスに職員を派遣し、幹部や従業員から事情を聴取し、データセキュリティー上の違反があったかや、その深刻度を調べている。

中国政府は、米企業が所有するAIを介してデータを処理したことで、中国の軍や警察、企業に関する機密データが米国側に流出し、データセキュリティー関連法に違反した可能性を懸念しているという。CACとムーンショット、DeepSeekはインフォメーションのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

アンソロピックは今月公表した報告書で、ムーンショットやDeepSeekなどが、利用者に知らせないまま、自社のチャットボットに寄せられた質問をアンソロピックのクロードに送っていたと指摘した。

アンソロピックはさらに、ムーンショットが「蒸留」と呼ばれる手法を用いていたと主張。蒸留は、より高性能なAIモデルから得たデータを使って、性能の低いモデルを改良する手法だ。今回についてアンソロピックは、ムーンショットが同社のシステムから得た回答を、自社独自のソフトウエアの訓練に利用したとみている。

米安全保障当局は、DeepSeekやムーンショットを含む中国の主要AI企業が、蒸留を通じて米企業が持つ独自の知識を組織的に抽出していると指摘している。

原題：China Probes DeepSeek, Moonshot Over Data Security: Information

items.title: Trump urges complete isolation of Iran, expects deal after election
items.author: Michelle Nichols, Daphne Psaledakis
items.creator: Michelle Nichols, Daphne Psaledakis
items.summary: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday called for complete economic isolation of Iran, showing no intention to resume talks at the UN General Assembly but saying he believed a deal would be done after the US midterm elections in November.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday called for complete economic isolation of Iran, showing no intention to resume talks at the UN General Assembly but saying he believed a deal would be done after the US midterm elections in November.
Iran had earlier hinted at the prospect of reviving negotiations to end their almost seven-month-old conflict , with the presidents of both countries due at the UN in New York.
A senior Iranian official said Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz to Gulf shipping within seven days if the US fulfilled Tehran's demands to ease military pressure and lift an American blockade on Iranian ports, adding that Tehran had conveyed its latest proposal to Washington via mediators last week.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told NBC's "Today" show the US was open to speaking with the Iranians, "especially if it has the prospects of leading to something positive and ultimately achieving the goal of what this is all about".
But in a [USN:L1N45E0F9 TEXT:"combative speech"] to the UN, Trump gave no sign of readiness to compromise.
"I call on all nations to help to enforce the complete economic isolation of Iran," he said.
"I believe we'll make a deal right after the election because it doesn't make sense for them not to. They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election ."
IRAN SEES 'GOLDEN OPPORTUNITY' TO REVIVE DIPLOMACY The senior Iranian official had earlier told Reuters that the US should "announce that it wants to resolve the issue diplomatically, make that official, and then agree on a timeline".
"The UN General Assembly is a golden opportunity for the US to return to diplomacy," the official said.
No face-to-face meetings between Iran and the United States are known to have taken place since July, when an agreement on an interim deal to end the war collapsed weeks after it was signed.
In a reminder of Iran's firm position so far, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, who headed Iran's negotiating team at previous talks, said Iran would never surrender: "Trump must understand that he cannot impose his power on the Iranian people and its armed forces."
Trump was due to meet on Tuesday with leaders of the six Gulf Arab states: Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
All are keen to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the conduit for a fifth of global oil and gas shipments before the war, but wary of giving their longstanding rival Iran too much power.
All apart from Oman also host huge US military bases that have come under repeated Iranian attack throughout the war.
The biggest of them, Saudi Arabia, has been drawn deeper into the war this month, as Houthi fighters aligned to Iran have advanced in Yemen, routing forces of a Saudi-backed government and threatening Saudi oil exports through the Red Sea.
There was some relief on oil markets on Tuesday, after sources told Reuters that Saudi Arabia had restarted operations at its [USN:L1N45E09V TEXT:"East-West Pipeline"] and could resume exports within hours, albeit at reduced volume, from the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
The pipeline, Saudi Arabia's main alternative route for exports to bypass wartime disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, had been shut down after attacks this month that Riyadh blamed on Iranian allies in Iraq.
SAUDIS SEEK US SUPPORT AGAINST HOUTHIS The Houthis have driven back Saudi-supported government forces along the Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at its mouth, and have attacked Saudi Arabia directly with missiles and drones. The fighters are now pushing to seize the [USN:L1N45D0B1 TEXT:"strategic heights"] of the Kahboub Mountains that overlook the Red Sea coast.
The US, which bombed the Houthis for two months last year, has so far rebuffed repeated pleas from Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to rejoin the fight. The New York Times reported that Trump called off US strikes against the Houthis on Sunday at the last minute, after troops had already begun loading bombs onto planes.
Asked why Washington had held back from striking the Houthis, Rubio said: "Ultimately, if it comes down to it, the United States will always stand with Saudi Arabia and support them because we have an agreement with them to do so.
"That said, that is a very dangerous and complex conflict that pre-exists ... We have a history with the Houthis as well, and that's something we don't want to see impacted either."
On the table at the Gulf states' [USN:L1N45D0Z2 TEXT:"meeting with Trump"] is a Qatari proposal for a framework to bring Iran and the Arab Gulf states into a common security architecture, regional sources said. One source said Iran was reviewing the proposal.
Speaking at the Qatar Economic Forum in New York on Sunday, Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani said any such arrangement would need to provide security guarantees for the Gulf states and expand economic interdependence with Iran.
"Lasting security cannot be built through repeated cycles of escalations and retaliation, or arrangements that leave any state permanently exposed to insecurity," Sheikh Mohammed said.
(This story has been refiled to fix a typo in the headline.)

items.title: Five Adani group companies settle Sebi proceedings for ₹1.51 crore
items.author: Khushboo Tiwari
items.summary: Stock market regulator Sebi on Tuesday settled adjudication proceedings against five Adani group companies over alleged violations related to the disclosure of related-party transactions ...
items.body: Five Adani group companies have settled adjudication proceedings with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) for a cumulative amount of ₹1.51 crore on matters involving alleged lapses in disclosure of related-party transactions (RPTs). The case originated from Sebi’s examination into allegations of undisclosed RPTs and corporate governance lapses flagged in a report by now defunct Hindenburg Research. Under the settlement terms recommended by Sebi's High Powered Advisory Committee and accepted by the panel of whole-time members, Adani Enterprises paid ₹76.05 lakh, while Adani Green Energy paid ₹45.50 lakh. Adani Total Gas, AWL Agri Business, and Adani Energy Solutions each paid ₹9.75 lakh. Sebi had issued a show-cause notice (SCN) to the companies in February, 2024, alleging that Adani Enterprises had failed to disclose RPTs between its subsidiary Adani Estates and Vakoder Investment in its financial year 2012-13 (FY13) annual report as per the applicable accounting standard, in violation of the erstwhile listing agreement. Separately, the notice alleged that audit and limited review reports of several group companies for various quarters between 2015 and 2021 were signed by chartered accountancy firms Dharmesh Parikh & Co LLP and Shah Dhandharia & Co LLP without a valid peer review certificate, in violation of Sebi's listing obligations and disclosure requirement norms. “In view of the acceptance of the settlement terms and the receipt of settlement amount by Sebi, the instant adjudication proceedings initiated against the Applicants vide SCN dated February 15, 2024 is disposed of in terms of section 15JB of the SEBI Act and section 23JA of the SCRA read with regulation 23(1) of the Settlement Regulations on the basis of the settlement terms,” the settlement order dated September 22 noted. Earlier this month, Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) Managing Director Karan Adani and Chief Financial Officer B Ravi settled adjudication proceedings with the market regulator in a matter involving PMC Projects. Under the settlement mechanism, both paid ₹13.65 lakh each, following which the proceedings were disposed of. The settlement order on September 10 had stated that the investigations were in respect of the banking transactions and inter-corporate security deposits among PMC Projects (India) and APSEZ and its subsidiaries. Last year in September, Sebi had closed proceedings against Adani group companies, group Chairman Gautam Adani, and associated entities facing accusations of fund diversion, violations of RPTs, and fraud. In two separate orders, the regulator had exculpated the group in the matter of allegations made by short-seller Hindenburg Research in 2023, effectively bringing down curtains on the saga that had triggered a ₹12 trillion market-cap rout at the business group. The regulator held that transactions between Adani group companies and companies flagged by Hindenburg, including Adicorp Enterprises, Milestone Tradelinks, and Rehvar Infrastructure, could not be called RPTs. As a result, Sebi has held that other potential violations of regulatory norms around disclosures or fraud don’t stand.

PARIS, Sept 22 : French planemaker Dassault Aviation has flight-tested two new AI algorithms on its Rafale fighter jet, it said on Tuesday, in the latest sign of efforts by arms companies to incorporate the technology into future weapons systems.
The move comes as France prepares for the next generation of fighter jets or potential upgrades after the collapse of a Franco-German project with Airbus this year, and as Europe seeks greater autonomy in defence.
Dassault said it had tested an algorithm developed by its own engineers and a second one developed in collaboration with French defence technology group Thales. The two companies already cooperate on France's independent Rafale.
Dassault did not give details of the tests or the role of the algorithms, but described them as part of a broader initiative to integrate AI in support of human crews.

"They have reached a level of maturity that makes them eligible for future Rafale upgrades," the company said.
Arms companies worldwide are experimenting with AI to help pilots to make faster decisions and coordinate with uncrewed 'wingman' drones designed to fly alongside conventional jets.
Sweden's Saab said last year that it had conducted combat testing of a Gripen E warplane flown by AI against a real fighter pilot as it explores concepts for the next generation of combat jets.
In 2024, the Secretary of the US Air Force flew in a modified F-16 jet fitted with machine learning supplied by Shield AI to demonstrate the ability of AI to enter aerial battle with a crewed F-16.
Dassault has said it is capable of working on its own fighter jet while remaining open to cooperation with new partners.

items.title: 肥満症治療薬のノボノルディスク、薄毛治療分野への進出を模索
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 肥満症薬「ウゴービ」のメーカーであるデンマークの製薬会社ノボノルディスクは、消費者に直接販売する医薬品事業を拡大しようと、薄毛治療市場に注目している。

薄毛治療は依存症や更年期障害などとともに、ノボが自社の中核的な科学的専門知識、あるいは最近培われた処方薬を消費者に直接販売するノウハウと接点があるとみている分野の一つだ。

マーティン・ランゲ最高科学責任者（CSO）は22日のブルームバーグ主催のラウンドテーブルで、現在研究が進められている薄毛治療の科学の一部は、ホルモンの働きを調べる内分泌学を基にしており、ノボにはこの分野で長い歴史があると説明した。

ランゲ氏は「われわれの科学的知見を生かし、この分野に進出できる可能性はある」と述べ、「必ずしも最初に取り組む分野ではないが、明らかに可能性はあるだろう」と付け加えた。

急成長する肥満症治療薬市場でイーライリリーに首位の座を奪われたノボだが、肥満や糖尿病以外にも幅広い効果があるとみられるGLP-1受容体作用薬の用途をさらに広げたい考え。主力のウゴービと糖尿病治療薬の「オゼンピック」が2030年代の初めにかけて米国と欧州で特許が切れるのを前に、新たな成長分野を探っている。

同社は今週、投資家向け説明会で事業計画を示したが、具体的な内容に乏しいとして投資家は失望し、株価は急落した。

同社はまた、心臓病や肝疾患、血液疾患の新たな治療法も模索。補完的な買収を検討するとともに、社内の新薬開発パイプラインの迅速化も目指している。

ノボが薄毛治療市場に参入するとしても、時間はかかりそうだ。ランゲ氏は今年終盤または来年初めまでに中期段階の臨床試験に進めると見込まれる8つの疾患のリストを提示したが、薄毛治療は含まれていなかった。

競合の米イーライリリーも、女性医療など肥満症事業を補完し得る分野への進出を模索している。

原題：Ozempic Maker Novo Looks to Target Hair Loss in Consumer Push（抜粋）

items.title: CD&R and Warburg Pincus in joint bid for Canaccord Wealth, sources say
items.author: Amy-Jo Crowley
items.creator: Amy-Jo Crowley
items.summary: Private equity groups CD&R and Warburg Pincus are in talks to buy Canaccord Genuity’s British wealth arm, Canaccord Wealth, two people familiar with the matter said.
items.body:
Private equity groups CD&R and Warburg Pincus are in talks to buy Canaccord Genuity’s British wealth arm, Canaccord Wealth, two people familiar with the matter said.
The firms are in advanced discussions over a joint takeover after emerging as a leading bidder in an auction process [USN:L6N3VY0AG TEXT:"launched"] last year, the sources said.
Canaccord Wealth could be valued at more than 1 billion pounds ($1.34 billion), sources told Reuters in October 2025.
Spokespeople for CD&R and Warburg Pincus declined to comment. Canaccord Genuity and Canaccord Wealth did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
There has been a string of deals in the UK in the wealth management and financial advice market in recent years as firms look for greater scale and attempt to capitalise on rising demand for wealth services. Britain's NatWest Group [USN:L4N3Z50CX TEXT:"earlier"] this year bought Evelyn Partners for 2.7 billion pounds ($3.6 billion).
Fenchurch, a boutique investment bank, has been advising Canaccord Genuity on the sale, sources previously told Reuters. BlackRock-owned private credit firm HPS, which has held a minority stake in Canaccord Wealth since 2021, was expected to offload its shares as part of a sale, the report added.
Canaccord Wealth provides investment management, financial planning and wealth advisory services to private clients in Britain and internationally.

Curious case of Pakistani prof Junaid Hafeez—blasphemy, ‘secret’ Facebook group, death penalty

Junaid Hafeez was accused of hosting Qaisra Shahraz, a prominent British-Pakistani novelist, as a guest speaker at Bahauddin Zakariya University and endorsing her allegedly blasphemous remarks.

Debdutta Chakraborty

22 September, 2026 05:17 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Junaid Hafeez went to the United States on a Fulbright scholarship at Jackson State University in Mississippi | Photo: Facebook

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

New Delhi: Pakistan has never really hanged anyone for blasphemy. In author Mohammed Hanif’s words, the country simply fits a noose around a man’s neck each morning and loosens it each night — a mercy just enough to let the country’s conscience sleep. Pakistani professor Junaid Hafeez has been wearing that noose for 13 years.

Pakistanis have used multiple adjectives for him — promising, brilliant, a self-proclaimed romantic who loves books, poetry, and music, and a prisoner of conscience. None of it has helped him be acquitted. He remains in solitary confinement serving a death sentence since 2019. Both inside and outside the jail, his life remains in danger. 

Hafeez, a former visiting lecturer of English literature at Bahauddin Zakariya University in Multan, was arrested in March 2013, and accused of blasphemy for operating a secret Facebook group. 

Show Full Article

Hafeez was also accused of hosting Qaisra Shahraz, a prominent British-Pakistani novelist, as a guest speaker at Bahauddin Zakariya University and endorsing allegedly blasphemous remarks made during the lecture. Shahraz had to flee the country. 

In December 2019, after six years of adjournments and the transfer of judges, a trial court sentenced Hafeez to death. The Lahore High Court is scheduled to hear his case on Tuesday and rights activists are yet again calling for his release. 

In a video shared on X on Monday , activist Sheema Kermani called for a fair trial and his release. During the CJP protests in India, which saw a wave of support from Pakistan, author Mohammed Hanif called Hafeez a “Pakistan’s cockroach ” who has been behind bars, forgotten. 

The trial itself has become one of the most contentious cases in Pakistan’s legal history. Rashid Rehman, the lawyer who first took on Hafeez’s defence, was threatened openly in court by clerics and lawyers before he was shot dead in his office in 2014. In the years after, Hafeez was held in solitary confinement due to repeated attacks by other inmates, and the proceedings have been held behind closed doors, inside a high-security prison in Multan out of public view. 

According to his current lawyer, the case against him never came together. “The prosecution, the witnesses and trial could not prove any of the allegations,” the lawyer told The Guardian after Hafeez’s 2019 verdict. 

He recalled visiting Hafeez the night before the verdict and finding him almost lighthearted and certain, as everyone around him seemed to be, that acquittal was close.

What unfolded, however, the next day was what the lawyer described as “unprecedented”. Rather than presenting concrete evidence, the prosecutor told the judge that Hafeez was “against Islam” and reminded the court that the case was “sensitive”. 

“It was the point I realised they were just using the religious card,” the lawyer added, “which was an immoral and unethical precedent in the court.”

“Pakistan’s blasphemy laws operate as black laws—draconian, anachronistic statutes completely devoid of statutory safeguards and weaponised for personal or ideological vendettas. The case of academic Junaid Hafeez exposes how these edicts systematically dismantle judicial independence,” Pakistani lawyer Shafiq Ahmed told ThePrint.

“By substituting rigorous evidentiary standards with populist intimidation and silencing the defence through targeted terror, these laws strip citizens of their constitutional right to a fair trial. For the legal community, Hafeez’s conviction and his agonizing 13 years behind bars remain a grim indictment of a criminal justice system that routinely capitulates to majoritarian veto,” he added. 

From Jackson to jail
As a student, Hafeez initially studied medicine at Pakistan’s oldest medical college, the King Edward Medical University , in Lahore, but left after his first year to pursue English literature at Bahauddin Zakariya University, where he reportedly broke a decades-old academic record.

In 2009, he went to the United States on a Fulbright scholarship at Jackson State University in Mississippi , where he studied American literature, photography, and theatre. He returned to Pakistan in 2011, and became a visiting lecturer in the English department at his alma mater. He taught literature and invited outside speakers to the campus, including women’s rights activists.

Before his arrest, Islamist student groups had objected to what they described as his liberal teaching. Even finding a lawyer willing to represent Hafeez proved extraordinarily difficult. His father, Hafeez-ul Naseer, in a 2016 Dawn article recalled approaching one lawyer only to see him confronted by a large group of lawyers protesting his decision to take the case. 

Naseer talked about how he would take books for Hafeez to read from his personal collection, which the family said contained more than 6,000 volumes. By the time the trial court sentenced Hafeez to death in December 2019, he had already spent more than six years in prison.

The burden of blasphemy in Pakistan
In Pakistan, accusations of blasphemy can carry consequences beyond the courtroom. According to a Human Rights Watch report, over 1,500 blasphemy cases have been lodged since the 1980s. Most turn out to be fabricated.

Human rights organisations have documented cases in which accusations have been accompanied by threats, mob violence, or attacks on those who defend the accused. Two prominent Pakistani figures who advocated changes to the blasphemy laws — former Punjab Governor Salman Taseer and former federal minister Shahbaz Bhatti — after a Christian woman, Aasia Bibi, was wrongfully convicted of blasphemy, were both assassinated in 2011.

That history hangs over Hafeez’s appeal. When an August 2026 Reuters report claimed that blasphemy cases had gone down under Pakistan’s de facto head, Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, many were quick to highlight Hafeez’s case.  

Ahmad Noorani, a Pakistani journalist, described the broader problem in stark terms. In his view, Hafeez’s case cannot be separated from the wider evolution of Pakistani society and the political use of religious sentiment. In the 80s, General Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq rewrote colonial-era blasphemy laws. His amendments tightened the hold of Sunni clerics and named specific offences like desecrating the Quran and insulting the Prophet’s companions. He outlawed Ahmadis from even calling themselves Muslim. The punishment was changed from 2-3 years to life imprisonment or death. 

“What happens when a state is built on religion? The country was founded on a premise that a nation could be built on the basis of religion and a few years later, that premise produced the man suited to carry it to its logical end: Zia-ul-Haq. Everything he did to this society — the fracturing, the unravelling — followed from that founding choice,” said Noorani.

“Hafeez, a well-educated man, a professor, was accused of something he almost certainly didn’t do, but the accusation itself made justice impossible. No lawyer could represent him and remain in the city. Any lawyer who tried was driven out. And when one finally came from elsewhere — Rashid Rehman — he was killed for it. Sit with that. Consider how hollow, how manufactured a case has to be, that the people behind it needed to remove every honest voice from the room before it could proceed,” he added . 

“This is what happens when you build a state on religion or build it on something else entirely and dress it in religion’s colours afterward. The wound doesn’t stay contained to one courtroom. It spreads,” he added.

Qindeel Azeem, a human rights activist who recently spoke to Hafeez’s lawyer, described Hafeez, now in his 40s, as a man who has developed mental health issues after years of imprisonment. His solitary confinement has itself become a form of punishment. His family has aged outside the prison walls. His father, now almost 70, refuses to give up. His mother has largely withdrawn from ordinary life. 

“The real challenge right now is that he appeal in the high courts is heard,” Azeem said.

“There’s a pattern we’ve watched for years — a date gets set, and then charges get quietly altered, or the paperwork ‘isn’t available,’ or the date just moves” .

She is hopeful they will see an acquittal this time. “It’s been years. Hafeez’s lawyer, Saif ul-Malook, is genuinely hopeful, that they’re finally about to hear it. And if they do, there’s a real chance he’s acquitted.”

According to her, what the lower courts want to avoid isn’t a wrongful conviction, it’s the fallout from an acquittal. She pointed to the Aasia Bibi case as the template: “Every time one of these ends in acquittal, right-wing factions of society are unwilling to accept the verdict. Years of indoctrination have resulted in radicalism where there is no differentiation between the innocent and the guilty. It doesn’t matter what the court finds. In the public’s mind, the verdict was already decided the day the accusation was made. That’s the narrative, and everyone in power has learned to tiptoe around it rather than confront it.”

Hafeez and his family meanwhile wait. His trial was relisted for a later date on Tuesday by the Lahore High Court.

As a Pakistani writer, Saki Nama, wrote on Facebook: “Among many other national sins, this one looks the gravest of all.”

items.title: PREVIEW Motor racing-After karting fun, Verstappen looks to keep winning feeling going in Baku
items.author: Abhishek Takle
items.creator: Abhishek Takle
items.summary: Red Bull’s four-time champion Max Verstappen, fresh from a last-to-first karting triumph, will be looking to keep that winning feeling going by chalking up a first Formula One victory of the year at this weekend’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
items.body:
Red Bull’s four-time champion Max Verstappen, fresh from a last-to-first karting triumph, will be looking to keep that winning feeling going by chalking up a first Formula One victory of the year at this weekend’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
The Dutchman took just 14 laps and 35 minutes to scythe through a field of 100 competitors at Red Bull’s "Max vs. 100" karting challenge at Britain’s Silverstone last week.
That may have been nothing more than a fun exhibition event for the 71-times grand prix winner, who jokingly pointed out that it was his first win of the season.
But after six podium appearances, four in the last five races, and a second-place finish in Madrid Azerbaijan’s Baku street circuit could set the stage for Verstappen to break his victory duck for the year and become the venue’s first triple winner.
“Madrid was a good result for us and the team has been working hard on taking this positive momentum to make sure we maximise the performance of the car in Baku,” said the 28-year-old.
“We've made some good steps with the car over the last few races and we have some good memories here,” he added.
The Baku street track, a 6-km-long mix of flat-out blasts and tight corners, has a reputation for unpredictable races.
Seven different drivers have won the nine races at the venue, with Verstappen and former Mexican team mate Sergio Perez the only two to have won there more than once.
With safety cars a regular feature of the race, Verstappen’s victory hopes may well rest on Red Bull’s ability to take on the might of Mercedes. The team’s runaway championship leader Kimi Antonelli heads into the weekend gunning for a third straight win and ninth of the season.
The 20-year-old Italian, who won his home race at Monza from the back of the grid and followed that up with victory in the Spanish Grand Prix at the Madring, is 81 points clear of Briton George Russell, his team mate and closest title rival, after 14 rounds.
Russell and third-placed Ferrari rival Lewis Hamilton have both ruled themselves out of realistic title contention.
ANTONELLI CLOSING ON TITLE A win in Baku would only tighten Antonelli’s grip on the championship and move his prospect of becoming the first Italian to win a Formula One title since Alberto Ascari in 1953 further into the realm of when rather than if.
McLaren’s reigning champion Lando Norris, meanwhile, will be fired up to make up for the win that got away from him.
The Briton had been leading comfortably from pole in Madrid and seemed on course for his third win from four races when an ill-timed virtual safety car went against him. He eventually had to settle for third.
French racer Isack Hadjar will return to action alongside Verstappen after recovering from a wrist injury that sidelined him for the last three races. Yuki Tsunoda is set to step back into his reserve role.
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the first of a "triple header" of races on consecutive weekends, is being run on Saturday this year with the country marking its Remembrance Day on Sunday.
Organisers are also celebrating a "Decade of Racin" in Baku, with the race joining the Formula One calendar in 2016 as the European Grand Prix. This year’s race will be the 10th around the Baku street track, with the event left off the calendar during the COVID pandemic in 2020.

items.title: Trump warns in UN speech he could 'annihilate' Iran without peace deal
items.author: Gram Slattery, Humeyra Pamuk
items.creator: Gram Slattery, Humeyra Pamuk
items.summary: US President Donald Trump used his UN General Assembly speech on Tuesday to make the case for his war on Iran, arguing he has prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and warning that he could "annihilate the Islamic Republic" if no deal is reached to end the conflict.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump used his UN General Assembly speech on Tuesday to make the case for his war on Iran, arguing he has prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and warning that he could "annihilate the Islamic Republic" if no deal is reached to end the conflict.
While predicting his administration would strike a peace deal with Iran following the November 3 US midterm elections, Trump called on other nations to join America in isolating Iran economically to force it to the negotiating table.
"I have a big decision to make. Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?" Trump said. "Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?"
Since returning to office last year for a second term, Trump has sent waves through the global order, joining Israel to attack Iran, ordering a raid on Venezuela that captured the country's leader, and threatening to seize Greenland.
In a 37-minute speech, Trump laid out his foreign policy vision, contending that the war with Iran would spare the world the threat of a nuclear-armed menace while maintaining that US military dominance in the Western Hemisphere was essential to preventing crises from taking root.
"Our actions in Venezuela are proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere," Trump said. "While others have spoken of peace, I have made peace."
Outside the UN headquarters, dozens of anti-Iranian-government demonstrators gathered, a few of them holding up signs calling for democracy and decrying dictatorship.
Trump brushed aside suggestions that the midterm elections, in which his Republican Party risks losing control of Congress, could constrain his handling of the war. Some analysts have argued that a Democratic takeover of the legislature would weaken his leverage in the conflict.
"What they don't realize is that I'm not running," Trump said, referring to the leadership in Tehran. “I did that already, and won in a landslide. We won in a giant landslide, and I'll be here for 2-1/2 years.”
DIPLOMATIC WHIRLWIND Taking aim at US neighbors, Trump labeled Mexico "the epicenter of cartel violence," urged its government to "reclaim control of its soil," and said his administration was pursuing "a fundamental change in the situation in Cuba."
Members of the Cuban delegation walked out of the hall as Trump referenced his pressure campaign against the country.
"It's an absolutely failed state, it's failing like never before, and it will fall," said Trump, adding that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was overseeing negotiations with the US neighbor.
"We will not allow a haven for foreign adversaries to threaten America on our own doorstep, right at our doorstep."
Yet Trump's appearance was less dramatic than in 2025, when he used a combative speech to chastise world leaders, warning that some countries were "going to hell," and complained about UN facilities after being briefly stranded on a malfunctioning escalator and suffering an initial teleprompter failure.
Trump renewed his criticism of the UN, highlighting his efforts to cut its bureaucracy, but offered no fresh attacks or indications that the US would leave any additional UN agencies.
Trump spoke less than a week after a UN fact-finding mission said it had reasonable grounds to believe US forces committed war crimes in two strikes on Iran, including one that hit a primary school in the southern city of Minab.
He renewed his criticism of international bodies that could serve as a check on US power, singling out the International Criminal Court and declaring that US military personnel would not be subject to its authority.
"We will never allow US service members or anyone else to be investigated or given show trials by an anti-American tribunal with no jurisdiction over us," he said.
Ahead of a UN Security Council meeting on AI and international security on Wednesday, Trump acknowledged the challenges of the new technology but said "I'm not going to stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution."
The speech kicked off a day of high-level diplomacy at the United Nations, where Trump was due to meet more than a dozen world leaders as wars in the Middle East and Ukraine continued to test his foreign policy agenda.
After his speech, Trump was scheduled to meet with no fewer than 11 world leaders, including British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, Venezuela's interim leader Delcy Rodriguez, and the representatives of the Gulf states of the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait and Qatar.

items.title: Global biofuel output to jump nearly 70% by 2030 due to Gulf energy crisis, study finds
items.author: May Angel
items.creator: May Angel
items.summary: Global biofuels output is expected to surge nearly 70% by 2030 from 2025 levels as major producing countries push ahead with raising blending mandates in response to the energy crisis triggered by the Iran war, a study published on Tuesday found.
items.body:
Global biofuels output is expected to surge nearly 70% by 2030 from 2025 levels as major producing countries push ahead with raising blending mandates in response to the energy crisis triggered by the Iran war, a study published on Tuesday found.
The study was co-authored by London-based think tank Chatham House and non-profit certification group the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC).
Biofuels such as ethanol can be produced from a range of organic feedstocks but are typically made from food crops or animal feed. They are commonly blended with gasoline or diesel and become more competitive as fossil fuel prices rise.
The fuels have long been at the centre of debate over whether they help tackle climate change or contribute to food inflation and deforestation. The study's authors warned that the latest surge in demand risks worsening the latter.
"By prioritizing energy security in the short term, some policy responses may be trading off against increased food insecurity in the medium term (and) any additional shock such as extreme weather could severely affect food prices," they said.
Countries including Brazil, China, India, Indonesia and the US, along with the European Union, have proposed or adopted higher biofuel blending mandates since the outbreak of the Iran war.
The authors estimate that if all proposed mandates are fully implemented, the land needed to produce biofuel feedstocks could more than double by 2030 compared with 2023 levels. That would require an additional 36 million hectares, an area roughly the size of Germany.
"The speed at which biofuel mandates are being increased creates significant risks as demand for feedstocks may rise faster than environmental safeguards, certification systems, land-use planning and enforcement mechanisms can be implemented," the authors said.
They said feedstocks grown on degraded land or between crop seasons can help reduce land degradation and even restore land, but that is not typically the case for conventional, or first-generation, biofuels.
First-generation biofuels are made from food and feed crops such as corn and sugarcane. Second-generation, or advanced, biofuels are produced from organic residues and waste materials such as used cooking oil.
"Production of feedstocks for first-generation biofuels tends to have net negative consequences for land degradation, food security and water use," the authors said.
Crude oil prices have risen nearly 40% since the Iran war began in late February, while sugar and corn prices have gained about 20%.

items.title: DoorDash to pay $131.5 million to resolve New York City probe over delivery workers' pay
items.author: Jonathan Stempel
items.creator: Jonathan Stempel
items.summary: DoorDash said on Tuesday it will pay $131.5 million to settle a New York City government probe that found the food delivery company underpaid or waited too long to pay workers.
items.body:
DoorDash (DASH.O) said on Tuesday it will pay $131.5 million to settle a New York City government probe that found the food delivery company underpaid or waited too long to pay workers.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the settlement the city's largest labor enforcement action. It advances the city's longstanding effort to hold food delivery companies to a 2023 law intended to improve pay for delivery workers.
The accord also came nearly eight months after the city's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection accused DoorDash and rival Uber Eats (UBER.N) of engineering "design tricks" to deprive workers of more than $550 million in tips.
DoorDash will provide nearly $115 million of relief to about 264,000 workers, whom it calls Dashers, with a median payout of about $48. It accepted a $16.7 million civil fine.
"Simply put, we screwed up," San Francisco-based DoorDash said in a statement. "Our mistakes meant some Dashers were underpaid or paid late. While these mistakes weren't intentional, that doesn't make them okay."
Shares of DoorDash rose 0.2% in afternoon trading.
The payout includes $83 million to resolve a dispute over how to calculate pay for workers who were logged into the company's app but not actually making deliveries. Another $12.3 million addresses payments that were missed or arrived days or weeks late.
DoorDash also agreed to send detailed pay data to the city every month for three years.
MAYOR FAULTS 'GREEDY ALGORITHMS' At a press conference, Mamdani called the settlement "part of a larger commitment to hold delivery companies accountable."
He said DoorDash, through its use of "greedy algorithms," failed to comply with the 2023 city law intended to improve pay for delivery workers.
"For years, DoorDash failed to count every hour worked by delivery workers," Mamdani said. "This was not a rounding error or an accidental mistake."
City officials declined to address whether Uber Eats and the delivery app Grubhub are complying with the 2023 law.
Uber declined to comment. Grubhub did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
DoorDash said many errors resulted from deliveries that crossed city boundaries, had multiple pickup or drop-off locations, or were only partially fulfilled or canceled.
It said other errors resulted from technical bugs, or having incomplete banking information for workers. The company said it has fixed technical issues that caused the mistakes.
DoorDash, Uber Eats and Grubhub have had multiple legal battles with New York City, including challenges to its tipping laws and whether they must share customers' data with restaurants.

items.title: 原油下落､サウジがパイプライン再開を計画-ホルムズ巡る外交にも期待
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 22日のエネルギー市場では原油が下落。サウジアラビアが主要パイプラインを経由する輸送の再開を模索しているほか、ホルムズ海峡の再開に向けた外交努力が活発化する兆しも見られた。

北海ブレント原油は、一時1バレル＝98ドルを下回った。事情に詳しい関係者によると、サウジアラビアは今週の再稼働を視野にパイプラインの試験を実施しており、紅海沿岸のヤンブー港での積み出しも今週再開する見通しだという。

サウジの東西パイプラインは日量最大700万バレルの輸送能力を持ち、ホルムズ海峡を迂回する主要な輸送ルートとして利用されてきたが、今月ドローン攻撃を受けて停止していた。

また、ホルムズ海峡を巡る共同通信のニュースも手掛かりとなった。共同がイラン政府高官の話を基に報じたところによれば、イランは米国による港湾封鎖が解除されれば、7日以内にホルムズ海峡を再開するとの考えを米国側に示した。

また、イラン革命防衛隊は、国益にかなうのであれば交渉する必要があるとの見解を示したと国営イラン通信（IRNA）が伝えた。

ロンドン時間午前11時38分時点で、ブレント原油は2.5%安の1バレル＝97.81ドル。米ウェスト・テキサス・インターミディエート（WTI）は2.6%下げて93.28ドル。

items.title: Oro cae mientras operadores fortalecen apuestas a tasas altas por más tiempo
items.author: Pablo Sinha
items.creator: Pablo Sinha
items.summary: Los precios del oro bajaron el martes, ya que los mercados apuestan por una política más restrictiva de la Reserva Federal este año, mientras también siguen de cerca el conflicto en Oriente Medio.
items.body:
Los precios del oro bajaron el martes, ya que los mercados apuestan por una política más restrictiva de la Reserva Federal este año, mientras también siguen de cerca el conflicto en Oriente Medio.
* El oro al contado bajó un 0,4%, a 4.325,03 dólares la onza, a las 1610 GMT, mientras que los futuros del oro en Estados Unidos caían un 0,5%, a 4.362 dólares.
* "El problema sigue siendo que, pese a que el crudo muestra una leve tendencia a la baja, el mercado sigue descontando con fuerza las alzas de tasas de la Fed (...) En los últimos días hemos visto cierta fortaleza del dólar, lo que suele ser negativo para el oro", dijo Bart Melek, de TD Securities.
* Según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, los operadores estiman que hay un 90% de probabilidades de que se produzca un aumento de tasas en diciembre.
* Los mercados se centraron en el endurecimiento de la política monetaria, ya que el presidente de la Fed de San Luis, Alberto Musalem, y el de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, abogaron por nuevas alzas para reducir la inflación derivada de la fuerte demanda y el encarecimiento de la energía.
* Desde que estalló la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán a fines de febrero, el incremento de los precios de la energía ha avivado los temores inflacionistas, lo que ha obligado a los bancos centrales de todo el mundo a adoptar posturas de política monetaria restrictivas.
* Esto, a su vez, ha ejercido presión sobre los precios del oro, que han caído más de un 22% desde que tocaron un máximo histórico de 5.594,82 dólares por onza en enero.
* En otros metales preciosos, la plata al contado bajó un 0,5%, a 65,68 dólares; el platino ganó un 0,7%, a 1.810,81 dólares; y el paladio perdió un 1,1%, a 1.286,91 dólares.

items.title: FIFA's Infantino letter is ploy for re-election, says German FA chief
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A letter from FIFA President Gianni Infantino this week to all 211 members, offering to discuss reforms within world soccer's governing body, amid an ongoing crisis over his failed plan to sell a stake in the World Cup, is a mere ploy to get himself re-elected, Germany's Football Association (DFB) President Bernd Neuendorf said on Tuesday.
items.body:
A letter from FIFA President Gianni Infantino this week to all 211 members, offering to [USN:L1N45D0SB TEXT:"discuss reforms"] within world soccer's governing body, amid an ongoing crisis over his failed plan to sell a stake in the World Cup, is a mere ploy to get himself re-elected, Germany's Football Association (DFB) President Bernd Neuendorf said on Tuesday.
In Monday's letter seen by Reuters, Infantino proposed an independent review of FIFA's decision-making process, in a move that could help him regain support after the withdrawal of his controversial private investment plan.
Striking a conciliatory tone, he also said he would propose consultations with confederations, member associations and other stakeholders about strengthening FIFA's decision-making.
Infantino faced a fierce backlash over his proposal to sell a 20% stake in FIFA's commercial rights, including the World Cup, to private investors. The plan was [USN:L1N43X04P TEXT:"abandoned"] in July after strong opposition and boycott threats, with UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF calling for changes to FIFA's leadership.
CHANGE IS NECESSARY They had said there had been no consultation with any continental confederation at any stage, with Infantino acting alone. UEFA has said a change in leadership was now necessary with the European body having lost faith in the current president.
"I regard Gianni Infantino’s letter as a transparent ploy to secure his re-election next year," said DFB President Neuendorf on Tuesday. "Fundamentally, FIFA now seems to have recognised that changes are essential.
"However, Gianni Infantino is definitely not the right person to lead a reform process. He has squandered all credibility.“ Neuendorf is also a member of the FIFA Council, the organisation's main decision-making body.
Infantino also said in the letter that member associations' positions on proposals or governance matters would not affect their treatment by FIFA, whose development and solidarity programmes would continue under existing rules.
The Swiss is up for re-election in March next year, with his opponents [USN:L6N4520VY TEXT:"struggling"] to find a candidate to challenge the president. Sources familiar with the discussions told Reuters this month that he still had enough votes to win, prompting opponents to focus on curbing his powers.
'NOT RESTORED TRUST,' SAYS DUTCH FA The Dutch Football Association (KNVB) echoed the sentiments.
"For us, this has not restored trust," a Dutch FA spokesperson was quoted as saying by ANP news agency.
"The proposed actions are partly in line with our call for reforms within FIFA. Practice will show whether that is actually the case.
The KNVB, one of FIFA's founding members in 1904, last month had said it wants to host an international summit in Amsterdam to completely overhaul FIFA, calling for Infantino to be replaced by 2027 as part of sweeping reforms in the organisation.
"At the same time, the proposals cannot be viewed separately from the (public) pressure, and they would not have emerged without the current dynamics," the spokesperson added.

items.title: AI infrastructure firm Accelevation targets up to $5.4 billion valuation in US IPO
items.author: Pragyan Kalita
items.creator: Pragyan Kalita
items.summary: Accelevation is targeting a valuation of up to $5.37 billion in its US initial public offering, the data center infrastructure company said on Tuesday, joining a wave of firms tapping investor demand for AI-linked stocks.
items.body:
Accelevation is targeting a valuation of up to $5.37 billion in its US initial public offering, the data center infrastructure company said on Tuesday, joining a wave of firms tapping investor demand for AI-linked stocks.
The Miamisburg, Ohio-based Accelevation and some selling shareholders are aiming to raise up to $720 million by offering 30 million shares priced between $20 and $24.
The fall IPO season began tentatively amid worries over surging bond yields and the first US interest-rate hike in three years, but a pipeline of big-name issuers points to a pickup in activity.
Nvidia-backed AI cloud firm Nscale filed for an IPO this month, while smart-ring maker Oura launched its roadshow this week. AI startup Anthropic is preparing for a potential blockbuster listing later this year.
The market is moving beyond treating AI infrastructure as a single hot theme and should become more selective as options grow, said Kat Liu, vice president at research firm IPOX.
“Investors are likely to pay more attention to where a company sits in the value chain, the quality of its backlog and how effectively strong demand translates into revenue, margins and cash flow.”
Founded in 2017, Accelevation designs, makes and installs power distribution, cooling and modular infrastructure for data center customers.
Demand for such equipment has surged as tech companies spend heavily to build the computing capacity needed to develop and run AI models. Forgent Power Solutions (FPS.N) , which makes electrical equipment for data centers and power grids, has gained about 40% since going public in [USN:L4N3Z120G TEXT:"February"].
Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs and BofA Securities, among others, are the underwriters for Accelevation's offering. It will list on Nasdaq under the symbol “ACCV."

items.title: Banks, telecoms weigh on FTSE 100; focus on US-Iran talks
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The UK's FTSE 100 edged lower on Tuesday as banks and telecoms stocks retreated, while investors awaited potential US-Iran talks after signs of improved oil flows in the Strait of Hormuz.
items.body:
The UK's FTSE 100 edged lower on Tuesday as banks and telecoms stocks retreated, while investors awaited potential US-Iran talks after signs of improved oil flows in the Strait of Hormuz.
The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) fell 0.29% to 10,708.33 points, while the midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) climbed 0.14%.
Investors are cautious ahead of potential US-Iran talks at the United Nations General Assembly this week after more supplies emerged through the strait over the weekend.
Oil prices fell to a two-week low as prospects for Gulf supplies improved, with Iran [USN:L1N45E0GD TEXT:"signalling"] it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and Saudi Arabia set to resume exports from its Red Sea port.
Heavyweight banks (.FTNMX301010) fell 1.63% after becoming the biggest gainers in the previous session, with HSBC (HSBA.L) falling 1.6% and Standard Chartered (STAN.L) sliding 2.9%.
Telecom stocks <.FTNMX151020 > also slipped 2.45%. BT Group (BT.L) led the losses with a 3.8% fall, while Vodafone (VOD.L) and Airtel Africa (AAF.L) dropped by 2.2% and 1.9% respectively.
Defensive consumer stocks offered support to the main index with Diageo (DGE.L) gaining 1.5% and Unilever (ULVR.L) rising 1.2%.
Among other stocks, home improvement retailer Kingfisher (KGF.L) climbed 12.4% after raising its full-year profit outlook following a 9.9% rise in first-half earnings.
British engineering firm Smiths Group (SMIN.L) rose 7.5% after it [USN:L6N45E06P TEXT:"beat"] expectations for its full-year operating profit and launched a process to sell its US asbestos liability.
Cell and gene therapy manufacturer Oxford Biomedica (OXB.L) rose 6% after posting a 9% year-on-year increase in first-half revenue.
A gauge of British [USN:S8N41008A TEXT:"factory orders"] rose this month to reach its highest level since July 2023, a survey showed, adding to recent signs of resilience in Britain's economy.
Britain's government [USN:L8N45E06Z TEXT:"borrowed"] more than expected in August, official data showed, pushing the financial year-to-date deficit further above forecasts and adding pressure on finance minister John Healey ahead of his first budget next month.

items.title: 英国政府、8月までに約1.7兆円の借り入れ超過－来年度予算に逆風増す
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 英国政府の借入額が、4月からの会計年度の最初の5カ月間で773億ポンドに拡大し、予算責任局（OBR）の予想を81億ポンド（約1兆7100億円）上回った。インフレ上昇によって歳出が膨らんだためで、来月に初の予算案発表を控えるヒーリー財務相には打撃だ。

8月単月の借り入れも183億ポンドと、予想の148億ポンドを上回った。

会計年度の最初の5カ月間の税収は、OBRの予測を11億ポンド上回った。しかし、歳出が予測を74億ポンド上回った。このうち、年金を含む社会保障費が24億ポンド、債務利払い費が20億ポンドを占めた。

英政府統計局（ONS）の上級統計官トム・デービス氏は「財政赤字は昨年8月から約2割増加した。政府収入以上に支出が増えたためで、一部にはインフレの影響が出ている」と述べた。

借入額の拡大で、ヒーリー氏が予算案の策定を進める上で直面する課題が改めて明らかになった。同氏は予算案を通じてバーナム首相の経済構想を示すと同時に、政府借り入れが引き続き制御されていることを示し、神経質になっている債券市場を安心させる必要がある。

バーナム首相は、防衛や地方分権から住宅建設、社会福祉に至るまで野心的な計画を打ち出しているが、政策を実施する余地は極めて限られている。イラン戦争を一因とした借り入れコストの上昇により、財政ルールに対して確保していた236億ポンドの余力の半分がすでに失われたと推計されている。

家計がエネルギー料金の大幅な上昇に備える中、生活費を支援する追加策を打ち出すよう、バーナム氏への圧力も強まっている。同氏は、近く発表する予算案が「厳しい」ものになると認めている。

キャピタル・エコノミクスの英国担当副チーフエコノミスト、ルース・グレゴリー氏は、政府借入額の拡大について、歯止めのかからない支出の「惨たんたる状況」を示していると評した。同氏は近く発表される予算案について、「大規模な予算ではなく、小－中規模の増税・歳出措置を盛り込んだ予算となる可能性の方が高く、大幅な増税を避けるために首相の政策構想の多くが抑制されるとみている」と語った。

items.title: サウジ東西パイプライン稼働再開、紅海側で石油輸出22日にも開始
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［シンガポール／ニューデリー　２２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［シンガポール／ニューデリー　２２日　ロイター］ - サウジアラビアは原油を輸送する東西パイプラインの操業を再開した。西部の紅海沿岸のヤンブー港からの輸出は２２日中に再開する可能性がある。事情に詳しい複数の関係筋が明らかにした。

サウジは、ドローン（無人機）攻撃を受けて１３日に東西パイプラインを稼働を停止。ヤンブー港での原油積み出しも止まっていた。

関係筋によると、パイプラインは稼働再開したものの、流量は低水準にとどまっている。サウジアラムコは輸送量を日量４００万バレルに戻そうとしているという。治安筋は、完全再開には数週間かかる可能性があると述べた。

別の関係筋は、パイプラインの再開を受けて、紅海沿岸にあるアラムコの製油所向け原油供給も再開すると説明。２２日中にヤンブーで中国向けの原油タンカー１隻に積み込む予定だと述べた。

サウジの石油輸出再開に備え、商社は船舶間移送のためタンカーをエジプトの地中海沿岸にあるポートサイドやシディ・ケリールへ移動させているとされる。

サウジからの石油輸出再開の見通しとなり、北海ブレント先物は２ドル超下落し、９月８日以来の安値を付けた。［Ｏ／Ｒ］

items.title: TSX rises to two-week high on US-Iran talk hopes, tech gains
items.author: Avinash P, Darshan R
items.creator: Avinash P, Darshan R
items.summary:
Canada's main stock index rose on Tuesday, hitting a two-week high amid broad-based gains, as investors assessed the prospects of potential US-Iran talks at this week's UN meeting that could help bring an end to the six-month-old Middle East conflict.
The S&P/TSX Composite Index was up 0.6% at 36,242.73 points by 10:24 a.m. ET, the highest since September 8. Eight of the index's 10 main sectors were in the green.
items.body:
Canada's main stock index rose on Tuesday, hitting a two-week high amid broad-based gains, as investors assessed the prospects of potential US-Iran talks at this week's UN meeting that could help bring an end to the six-month-old Middle East conflict.
The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) was up 0.6% at 36,242.73 points by 10:24 a.m. ET, the highest since September 8. Eight of the index's 10 main sectors were in the green.
Iran and the United States hinted [USN:L1N45E0GD TEXT:"at the prospect of reviving negotiations"] to end their conflict on Tuesday, with presidents of both countries attending the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
The information technology sector (.SPTTTK) rose 2.3%, leading gains on the TSX, with e-commerce major Shopify (SHOP.TO) up nearly 8% and BlackBerry (BB.TO) up 2.8%.
Oil prices fell below $100 a barrel to a two-week low, as prospects for Gulf supplies improved, with Iran signaling it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and Saudi Arabia set to resume exports from its Red Sea port.
Sliding oil prices dragged the energy sector (.SPTTEN) down 0.3%, after briefly touching its lowest in a month.
"Oil goes down, you have oil stocks going down. But you could see the other side of it, which is banks, tech and others go higher because of oil going down. So it has a positive and negative side," said Allan Small, senior investment advisor at Allan Small Financial Group with iA Private Wealth
Despite the recent pullback in oil prices, the broader energy sector has risen more than 45% year-to-date, helping drive gains in the TSX, which is up more than 14% so far this year, outperforming the US benchmark S&P 500's (.SPX) 13.5% gain.
The materials index (.GSPTTMT) gained 1.6%, tracking higher prices of base metals.
Investors will also watch retail sales data due on Thursday for signals on the health of Canadian consumers.
